value.zh: 父充，別有傳。
value.en: Her father Jia Chong has his own biography.
value.literal: Her father Chong has separate biography.

value.zh: 初，武帝欲為太子取衛瓘女，元后納賈郭親黨之說，欲婚賈氏。
value.en: Wu favored Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yang Yan pushed Jia kin.
value.literal: At first Emperor Wu wished crown prince to marry Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yuan listened to Jia and Guo faction urging marriage with Jia clan.

value.zh: 帝曰：「衛公女有五可，賈公女有五不可。
value.en: Wu said, “Wei’s girl scores five merits—Jia’s five flaws.
value.literal: Emperor said: “Lord Wei’s daughter has five goods—Lord Jia’s daughter five bads.

value.zh: 衛家種賢而多子，美而長白；
value.en: Weis are fertile and wise—fair and statuesque;
value.literal: Wei house breeds wise and many sons—beautiful, tall, fair;

value.zh: 賈家種妒而少子，醜而短黑。」
value.en: Jias are jealous and barren—dark and squat."
value.literal: Jia house breeds jealousy and few sons—ugly, short, dark.”

value.zh: 元后固請，荀顗、荀勖並稱充女之賢，乃定婚。
value.en: Yang Yan insisted; Xun Yi and Xun Xu praised Jia’s girl—the match closed.
value.literal: Empress Yuan pressed firmly—Xun Yi and Xun Xu together praised Chong’s daughter’s virtue—betrothal fixed.

value.zh: 始欲聘后妹午，午年十二，小太子一歲，短小未勝衣。
value.en: They first chose sister Wu—twelve, petite beside the heir.
value.literal: At first they wished to engage younger sister Wu—Wu twelve years old, one year younger than crown prince, too short for robes.

value.zh: 更娶南風，時年十五，大太子二歲。
value.en: They wed Nanfeng instead—fifteen, two years his senior.
value.literal: They switched to Nanfeng—then fifteen, two years elder than crown prince.

value.zh: 泰始八年二月辛卯[7]，冊拜太子妃。
value.en: On xinmao in early 272 she became crown princess [7].
value.literal: Eighth Taishi year second month xinmao [7]—invested crown princess.

value.zh: 妒忌多權詐，太子畏而惑之，嬪御罕有進幸者。
value.en: Jealous and scheming, she cowed the befuddled prince—other women seldom touched him.
value.literal: Jealous, crafty in intrigue—crown prince feared yet dazed—concubines rarely gained favor.

value.zh: 帝常疑太子不慧，且朝臣和嶠等多以為言，故欲試之。
value.en: Wu doubted the heir’s wit—He Qiao agreed—so he tested him.
value.literal: Emperor often suspected crown prince dull—and ministers such as He Qiao said same—so wished to test him.

value.zh: 盡召東宮大小官屬，為設宴會，而密封疑事，使太子決之，停信待反。
value.en: He feasted Eastern Palace staff, sealed riddling cases for the heir to solve.
value.literal: He summoned all eastern palace officials large and small, set banquet, sealed doubtful affairs ordering crown prince to decide—stopped courier awaiting reply.

value.zh: 妃大懼，倩外人作答。
value.en: Princess Jia panicked and outsourced answers.
value.literal: Consort greatly frightened—begged outsider compose answers.

value.zh: 答者多引古義。
value.en: Ghostwriters packed classics.
value.literal: Answerers mostly cited classical meanings.

value.zh: 給使張泓曰：「太子不學。
value.en: Clerk Zhang Hong warned, “He never studied.
value.literal: Orderly Zhang Hong said: “Crown prince does not study.

value.zh: 而答詔引義，必責作草主，更益譴負。
value.en: Classic prose exposes the ghostwriter.
value.literal: Yet reply edict cites meanings—surely will blame draft master—increasing blame.

value.zh: 不如直以意對。」
value.en: Plain speech fits better."
value.literal: Better answer straight from plain intent.”

value.zh: 妃大喜，語泓：「便為我好答，富貴與汝共之。」
value.en: She thrilled: "Write plainly for me—wealth and honor we will share."
value.literal: Consort rejoiced, telling Hong: "Answer well for me—wealth and honor shared with you."

value.zh: 泓素有小才，具草，令太子自寫。
value.en: Hong drafted; she made the prince copy.
value.literal: Hong always had small talent—drafted fully—ordered crown prince himself copy.

value.zh: 帝省之，甚悅。
value.en: Wu read it—delighted.
value.literal: Emperor examined—greatly pleased.

value.zh: 先示太子少傅衛瓘，瓘大踧踖，眾人乃知瓘先有毀言，殿上皆稱萬歲。
value.en: He flashed it at Wei Guan—Wei squirmed; courtiers jeered Guan’s prior slanders.
value.literal: First showed Junior Mentor Wei Guan—Guan greatly ashamed—all knew Guan earlier had slanderous words—hall cheered ten thousand years.

value.zh: 充密遣語妃云：「衛瓘老奴，幾破汝家。」
value.en: Jia Chong whispered to the consort, "Old slave Wei Guan nearly ruined your house."
value.literal: Chong secretly sent word to consort: "Old slave Wei Guan nearly ruined your house."

value.zh: 后暴戾日甚。
value.en: Her cruelty mounted daily.
value.literal: Consort violent cruelty daily worsened.

value.zh: 侍中賈模，后之族兄，右衛郭彰，后之從舅，並以才望居位，與楚王瑋、東安公繇分掌朝政。
value.en: Jia Mo and Guo Zhang ran court beside Sima Wei and Sima Yao.
value.literal: Palace Attendant Jia Mo—consort’s lineage elder; Guards-general Guo Zhang—consort’s maternal uncle—both by talent and prestige held posts sharing governance with Prince Chu Wei and Duke Dongan Yao.

value.zh: 后母廣城君養孫賈謐干預國事，權侔人主。
value.en: Lady Guo raised Jia Mi—his power rivaled the throne.
value.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng raised grandson Jia Mi meddling state affairs—authority matched sovereign.

value.zh: 繇密欲廢后，賈氏憚之。
value.en: Sima Yao plotted deposition—Jias feared him.
value.literal: Yao secretly wished depose consort—Jia faction feared him.

value.zh: 及太宰亮、衛瓘等表繇徙帶方，奪楚王中候，后知瑋怨之，乃使帝作密詔令瑋誅瓘、亮，以報宿憾。
value.en: When Sima Liang and Wei Guan banished Yao and clipped Wei’s guard—she forged orders for Sima Wei to murder Liang and Wei.
value.literal: When Grand Mentor Liang and Wei Guan memorialized to exile Yao to Daifang and strip Prince Chu of central army inspector—consort knew Wei bore grudge—had emperor forge secret edict ordering Wei to kill Guan and Liang—settling old hatred.

value.zh: 模知后凶暴，恐禍及己，乃與裴頠、王衍謀廢之，衍悔而謀寢。
value.en: Jia Mo saw danger—planned coup with Pei Yi—Wang Yan backed out.
value.literal: Mo knew consort fierce—feared disaster reaching himself—with Pei Yi and Wang Yan plotted deposition—Yan repented—plot slept.

value.zh: 初，后詐有身，內稿物為產具，遂取妹夫韓壽子慰祖養之，託諒闇所生，故弗顯。
value.en: She faked pregnancy—snatched Han Shou’s son Weizu—called him newborn heir.
value.literal: At first consort feigned pregnancy—packed straw goods as birthing gear—then took sister’s husband Han Shou’s son Weizu raising—claimed mourning-hall birth—therefore not openly shown.

value.zh: 遂謀廢太子，以所養代立。
value.en: She meant to replace the heir with him.
value.literal: Then plotted depose crown prince—establish fosterling.

value.zh: 時洛中謠曰：「南風烈烈吹黃沙，遙望魯國鬱嵯峨，前至三月滅汝家。」
value.en: Luoyang sang: "Nanfeng blasts yellow dust—far off Lu towers loom—by the third moon your house will fall."
value.literal: Then Luoyang rhyme said: "South wind fierce blows yellow sand—far gaze Lu kingdom towering—before third month ends your house."

value.zh: 后母廣城君以后無子，甚敬重愍懷，每勸厲后，使加慈愛。
value.en: Lady Guo prized Minhuai—begged Jia to cherish him.
value.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng because consort lacked sons greatly revered Crown Prince Minhuai—often urged consort—made her add kindness.

value.zh: 賈謐恃貴驕縱，不能推崇太子，廣城君恒切責之。
value.en: Jia Mi insulted the heir—Lady Guo scolded him.
value.literal: Jia Mi relied on pride—could not honor crown prince—Lady Guangcheng constantly scolded.

value.zh: 及廣城君病篤，占術謂不宜封廣城，乃改封宜城。
value.en: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—she became Princess Yicheng.
value.literal: When Lady Guangcheng gravely ill—divination said unsuitable enfeoff Guangcheng—thereupon changed enfeoff Yicheng.

value.zh: 后出侍疾十餘日，太子常往宜城第，將醫出入，恂恂盡禮。
value.en: Minhuai nursed her mother—deferential.
value.literal: Consort attended illness ten-plus days—crown prince often visited Yicheng mansion—brought physicians—obedient exhaustive ritual.

value.zh: 宜城臨終執后手，令盡意于太子，言甚切至。
value.en: She clasped Jia’s hand—beg her shield Minhuai.
value.literal: Yicheng dying grasped consort’s hand—ordered exhaust feeling toward crown prince—speech extremely earnest.

value.zh: 又曰：「趙粲及午必亂汝事，我死後，勿復聽入，深憶吾言。」
value.en: She also said, "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely disrupt your affairs; after I die, do not admit them again—remember my words well."
value.literal: Also said: “Zhao Can and Wu surely ruin your affairs—after I die—never hear them again—deeply remember my words.”

value.zh: 后不能遵之，遂專制天下，威服內外。
value.en: Jia ignored—ruled alone.
value.literal: Consort could not obey—thereupon monopolized realm—awe subdued inner and outer.

value.zh: 更與粲、午專為姦謀，誣害太子，眾惡彰著。
value.en: She schemed with them against Minhuai.
value.literal: Further with Can, Wu solely plotted wickedness—slandered harmed crown prince—crowds of evils manifest.

value.zh: 初，誅楊駿及汝南王亮、太保衛瓘、楚王瑋等，皆臨機專斷，宦人董猛參預其事。
value.en: Yang Jun, Sima Liang, Wei Guan, Sima Wei died by her whim—with eunuch Dong Meng.
value.literal: At first executing Yang Jun and Prince Runan Liang, Grand Tutor Wei Guan, Prince Chu Wei—all improvised executions—eunuch Dong Meng participated.

value.zh: 猛，武帝時為寺人監，侍東宮，得親信于后，預誅楊駿，封武安侯，猛三兄皆為亭侯，天下咸怨。
value.en: Dong Meng gained titles—his brothers too—the realm cursed them.
value.literal: Meng—Wu-era Inner Palace Overseer—served Eastern Palace—won consort trust—participated executing Yang Jun—enfeoffed Marquis Wu’an—Meng three elder brothers all village marquis—all realm resented.

value.zh: 元敬虞皇后
value.en: Empress Yu, posthumously titled Respectful and Reverent.
value.literal: Empress Yu the Yuanjing (Primordial Reverence).

value.zh: 史臣曰：方祇體安，儷乾儀而合德；
value.en: The historians write: Earth holds still and mates with Heaven's pattern, sharing its virtue;
value.literal: The historian's subject says: The square earth-spirit embodies tranquility; paired with Qian's model and joins virtue;

value.zh: 圓舒循晷，配羲曜以齊明。
value.en: the round moon follows the sundial's course and pairs with the solar splendor so both lights shine as one.
value.literal: the round unfolds following sundial; paired with Xi radiance thereby equal brightness.'

value.zh: 故知陽爍陰凝，萬物假其陶鑄；
value.en: Thus yang's fire and yin's mold shape all things through their forge;
value.literal: Therefore know yang melts yin congeals; the myriad things borrow their pottery-casting;

value.zh: 火炎水潤，六氣由其調理。
value.en: flame and flood temper the six cosmic breaths.
value.literal: fire flames water moistens; the six qi by them are regulated and ordered.'

value.zh: 取譬賢淑，作伉文思，靈根式固，實資於此。
value.en: Likewise wise consorts match cultured sovereigns, anchoring the sacred root—dynastic endurance depends on such unions.
value.literal: Taking comparison from worthy and pure; making mate civil reflection; spiritual root thereby firm; truly relies on this.'

value.zh: 宣穆閱禮，偶德潛鱗，翊天造之艱虞，嗣塗山之逸響，寶運歸其後胤，蓋有母儀之助焉。
value.en: Empress Xuanmu mastered ritual and matched her lord while he still hid like a dragon in the deep; she steadied him through peril and echoed the virtue of Tushan—later triumph rested with her line in part because she showed what a mother of the state should be.
value.literal: Xuanmu examined rites; paired virtue hidden fish-scale; assisted Heaven-making's hardship and anxiety; continued Tushan's lingering echo; precious fortune returned to her later descendants—probably had motherly model's assistance.

value.zh: 武元楊氏預聞朝政，明不逮遠，愛溺私情，深杜衛瓘之言，不曉張泓之詐，運其陰沴，韜映乾明，晉道中微，基于是矣。
value.en: Lady Yang of Wuyuan meddled in state affairs: foresight failed her, partial love swayed her, she silenced Wei Guan and never saw through Zhang Hong—the poison she spread dimmed the imperial house, and the decline of Jin began there.
value.literal: Lady Yang of Wuyuan participated in hearing dynastic government; brightness did not reach far; love drowned in private feeling; deeply blocked Wei Guan's words; did not comprehend Zhang Hong's deceit; wielded her sinister balefulness; concealed and dimmed Qian brightness; Jin's path waned in the middle—the foundation lay herein.

value.zh: 惠皇稟質，王縱其嚚，識暗鳴蛙，智昏文蛤。
value.en: Emperor Hui was dull by nature while the Wang women unleashed their malice—his wit was no brighter than a frog's croak, his judgment no sharper than a clam in mud.
value.literal: Emperor Hui received substance; consorts of Wang indulged their viciousness; insight dark as croaking frogs; wisdom dim as patterned clams.

value.zh: 南風肆狡，扇禍稽天。
value.en: Jia Nanfeng gave free rein to cunning and fanned disaster until it scraped the sky.
value.literal: South Wind wantonly cunning; fanning calamity reaching Heaven.

value.zh: 初踐椒宮，逞梟心于長樂；
value.en: Once she mounted to the pepper-scented halls she showed an owl's heart in Changle Palace;
value.literal: First treading the pepper palace; displaying owl heart in Changle;

value.zh: 方觀梓樹，頒鴆羽於離明。
value.en: then, watching the catalpa in court, she dealt death beneath the southern sun like spreading poisoned plumes.
value.literal: just viewing the catalpa tree; issuing owl-feathers at Li brightness.

value.zh: 褒后滅周，方之蓋小；
value.en: Baosi brought Zhou low—set beside Nanfeng she seems almost minor;
value.literal: Baosi destroyed Zhou; comparing her, roughly smaller;

value.zh: 妹妃傾夏，曾何足喻。
value.en: Mo Xi who drowned Xia is hardly fit as her mirror.
value.literal: Mo Xi overturned Xia—how could she suffice as comparison?

value.zh: 中原陷於鳴鏑，其兆彰於此焉。
value.en: The heartland would fall to whistling arrows—the omen was already plain in this.
value.literal: The Central Plain sank amid whistling arrows; its portent was manifest herein.

value.zh: 昔者高宗諒闇，總百官於元老；
value.en: Ancient Gaozong wore unhemmed sackcloth yet entrusted the hundred bureaus to his aged ministers;
value.literal: Formerly Gaozong in mourning hut; gathered hundred offices in elder ministers;

value.zh: 成王沖眇，託萬機於上公。
value.en: young King Cheng placed every weight of state upon the grand dukes.
value.literal: King Cheng young and tiny; entrusted myriad mechanisms to senior dukes.

value.zh: 太后御宸，諒知非古。
value.en: A dowager holding the purple palace was never classical precedent.
value.literal: Empress dowager controlling the celestial throne—indeed knowing it is not ancient.

value.zh: 而明穆、康獻，仍世臨朝，時屬委裘，躬行負扆。
value.en: Yet Empresses Mingmu and Kangxian ruled generation after generation when an emperor's cloak lay empty, sitting themselves against the imperial screen.
value.literal: Yet Mingmu and Kangxian, successive generations attended court; times belonged to letting-down robe; personally bore screen-back.

value.zh: 各免華陽之釁，竟躡和熹之蹤，保陵遲以克終，所幸實為多矣。
value.en: Each escaped the stain that befell Yang Zhi of Huayang, trod instead in Deng Sui's footsteps, and steered a fading court to a peaceful close—more good fortune than anyone might expect.
value.literal: Each avoided Huayang's blame; ultimately trod Hexi's tracks; preserved decline to achieve end—what was fortunately attained was indeed much.

value.zh: 陳騫
value.en: Chen Qian
value.literal: Chen Qian

value.zh: 楷子瓚娶楊駿女，然楷素輕駿，與之不平。
value.en: Zan's marriage to Jun's daughter strained Kai's contempt for Jun.
value.literal: Kai's son Zan married Yang Jun's daughter though Kai despised Jun.

value.zh: 駿既執政，乃轉為衛尉，遷太子少師，優遊無事，默如也。
value.en: Jun sidelined him as ceremonial tutor with nothing to do.
value.literal: Once Jun dominated court, Kai became minister of guards and junior tutor—idle, mute.

value.zh: 及駿誅，楷以婚親收付廷尉，將加法。
value.en: Jun's purge dragged Kai toward execution.
value.literal: When Jun fell, Kai as in-law went to the Ministry of Justice for sentencing.

value.zh: 是日事倉卒，誅戮縱橫，眾人為之震恐。
value.en: Sudden killings terrified everyone.
value.literal: That day slaughter raced everywhere—courtiers panicked.

value.zh: 楷容色不變，舉動自若，索紙筆與親故書。
value.en: He calmly penned letters while awaiting death.
value.literal: Kai never flinched; calmly he borrowed brush and wrote farewell letters.

value.zh: 賴侍中傅祗救護得免，猶坐去官。
value.en: Fu Zhi intervened; Kai merely lost rank.
value.literal: Thanks to Palace Attendant Fu Zhi's rescue he escaped execution, though he still lost office for it.

value.zh: 太保衛瓘、太宰亮稱楷貞正不阿附，宜蒙爵土，乃封臨海侯，食邑二千戶。
value.en: Wei Guan and Sima Liang restored him as marquis of Linhai.
value.literal: Grand tutors Wei Guan and Sima Liang praised Kai's integrity—he deserved a fief—and named him Marquis of Linhai with two thousand households.

value.zh: 代楚王瑋為北軍中候，加散騎常侍。
value.en: He took the northern army colonelcy alongside attendant honors.
value.literal: He replaced Prince Chu Wei as colonel of the northern armies plus supernumerary attendant.

value.zh: 瑋怨瓘、亮斥己任楷，楷聞之，不敢拜，轉為尚書。
value.en: Wei blamed Kai for stealing his command; Kai fled upward to the ministry.
value.literal: Wei resented Guan and Liang for ousting him for Kai; Kai declined the post and became minister of state.

value.zh: 楷長子輿先娶亮女，女適衛瓘子，楷慮內難未已，求出外鎮，除安南將軍、假節、都督荊州諸軍事，垂當發而瑋果矯詔誅亮、瓘。
value.en: Marriage ties to both factions drove Kai toward Jingzhou—Wei's forged orders struck first.
value.literal: Kai's heir Yu had first married Sima Liang's daughter, and Kai's daughter was married to a son of Wei Guan—fearing civil war Kai sought a province; made General Who Pacifies the South, with staff, commanding Jingzhou military affairs—just as he prepared to march, Wei forged an edict killing Liang and Guan.

value.zh: 瑋以楷前奪己中候，又與亮、瓘婚親，密遣討楷。
value.en: Wei sent killers after Kai for family links to his victims.
value.literal: Wei because Kai had earlier displaced him from Central Commander and was also marriage kin to Liang and Guan secretly sent forces against Kai.

value.zh: 楷素知瑋有望于己，聞有變，單車入城，匿于妻父王渾家，與亮小子一夜八徙，故得免難。
value.en: He dodged patrols by hiding with Wang Hun and Liang's orphan.
value.literal: Kai had always known Wei bore him ill will; hearing of the upheaval, he drove alone into the city and hid in his father-in-law Wang Hun's house; with Liang's youngest son he moved eight times in one night—thus he escaped harm.

value.zh: 瑋既伏誅，以楷為中書令，加侍中，與張華、王戎並管機要。
value.en: Wei fell and Kai joined Zhang Hua and Wang Rong at power's core.
value.literal: After Wei died Kai directed the palace secretariat with Zhang Hua and Wang Rong.

value.zh: 魏舒，字陽元，任城樊人也。
value.en: Wei Shu, whose courtesy name was Yangyuan, came from Fan in Rencheng commandery.
value.literal: Wei Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was a man of Fan in Rencheng.

value.zh: 少孤，為外家寧氏所養。
value.en: He lost his father while still young and was brought up by his mother's people, the Nings.
value.literal: In youth he was orphaned and was reared by his maternal kin, the Ning clan.

value.zh: 寧氏起宅，相宅者云：「當出貴甥。」
value.en: When the Nings raised a new house, a geomancer told them, "This site will produce a distinguished nephew."
value.literal: The Ning family built a house, and a geomancer of the site said, "A noble nephew will come forth."

value.zh: 外祖母以魏氏甥小而慧，意謂應之。
value.en: His maternal grandmother, seeing that the Wei boy was young but bright, assumed the omen pointed to him.
value.literal: His maternal grandmother, because the Wei nephew was small yet clever, in her mind thought it referred to him.

value.zh: 舒曰：「當為外氏成此宅相。」
value.en: Shu said, "It falls to me to fulfill that houselot prophecy for our mother's family."
value.literal: Shu said, "I shall for the maternal clan complete this houselot omen."

value.zh: 久乃別居。
value.en: Only after many years did he move out and keep a separate household.
value.literal: After a long time then he lived apart.

value.zh: 身長八尺二寸，姿望秀偉，飲酒石餘，而遲鈍質樸，不為鄉親所重。
value.en: He stood eight chi and two cun tall, carried himself with striking presence, and could put away more than a shi of wine, yet he seemed slow and unpolished, so neighbors and relatives thought little of him.
value.literal: His body was eight chi two cun in height, his bearing fine and grand, he drank more than a shi of wine, yet was slow, dull, plain, and was not esteemed by townsmen and kin.

value.zh: 從叔父吏部郎衡，有名當世，亦不之知，使守水碓，每歎曰：「舒堪數百戶長，我願畢矣！」
value.en: His paternal uncle Heng, a Personnel Ministry officer celebrated in their day, never recognized his gifts either and set him to mind the water-powered mill, sighing, "If Shu can serve as headman over a few hundred households, I shall ask nothing more!"
value.literal: His father's cousin Heng, Personnel Ministry gentleman, had fame in the age, also did not know him, made him guard the water trip-hammer, and often sighed, saying, "Shu can suffice as chief of several hundred households — my wishes are fulfilled!"

value.zh: 舒亦不以介意。
value.en: Shu did not resent him for it.
value.literal: Shu also did not on that account take it to mind.

value.zh: 不修常人之節，不為皎曆之事，每欲容才長物，終不顯人之短。
value.en: He scorned petty convention and avoided ostentatious moralism, preferring always to nurture others' strengths and never to expose their faults.
value.literal: He did not cultivate ordinary men's scruples, did not do bright-harsh matters, always wished to accommodate talent and lengthen things, and to the end did not display people's shortcomings.

value.zh: 性好騎射，著韋衣。
value.en: He loved riding and archery and habitually dressed in leather hunting clothes.
value.literal: By nature he loved riding and shooting, and wore leather garments.

value.zh: 入山澤，以漁獵為事。
value.en: He roamed hills and wetlands and made fishing and hunting his chief pastime.
value.literal: He entered mountains and marshes and took fishing and hunting as his occupation.

value.zh: 唯太原王乂謂舒曰：「卿終當為台輔，然今未能令妻子免饑寒，吾當助卿營之。」
value.en: Wang Yi of Taiyuan alone told him, "You are destined for the highest councils of state, yet you cannot yet keep your wife and children from want; let me help you set them up."
value.literal: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan said to Shu, "You in the end will become a pillar minister, yet now are not able to cause wife and children to escape cold and hunger; I shall help you arrange it."

value.zh: 常振其匱乏，舒受而不辭。
value.en: Wang regularly supplied what the household lacked, and Shu accepted without demur.
value.literal: He regularly relieved their want; Shu accepted and did not decline.

value.zh: 舒嘗詣野王，主人妻夜產，俄而聞車馬之聲，相問曰：「男也，女也？」
value.en: On a visit to Yewang, while his host's wife labored in the night, voices like chariots and horses suddenly sounded outside, asking, "Boy or girl?"
value.literal: Shu once went to Yewang; the host's wife gave birth in the night; presently they heard the sound of horses and chariots, mutually asking, "Male or female?"

value.zh: 曰：「男，書之，十五以兵死。」
value.en: The answer came: "A son. Record it—he will die by the sword at fifteen."
value.literal: It was said, "Male; write it; at fifteen he will die by weapons."

value.zh: 復問：「寢者為誰？」
value.en: Then they asked, "Who lies abed here?"
value.literal: Again they asked, "Who is the one sleeping?"

value.zh: 曰：「魏公舒。」
value.en: The reply was, "Lord Wei Shu."
value.literal: It was said, "Lord Wei Shu."

value.zh: 後十五載，詣主人，問所生兒何在，曰：「因條桑為斧傷而死。」
value.en: Fifteen years later he looked up the host and asked after that child; the man said, "He died when an axe slipped as he was pruning mulberry."
value.literal: After fifteen years he went to the host, asked where the born child was, and it was said, "Because trimming mulberry he was wounded by an axe and died."

value.zh: 舒自知當為公矣。
value.en: Shu understood then that he was fated to rise to the rank of duke.
value.literal: Shu himself knew he would become a duke.

value.zh: 太康初，拜右僕射。
value.en: Early in the Taikang era he was appointed right vice-director of the Masters of Writing.
value.literal: At the beginning of Taikang he was appointed Right Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 舒與衛瓘、山濤、張華等以六合混一，宜用古典封禪東嶽，前後累陳其事，帝謙讓不許。
value.en: Shu joined Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Zhang Hua, and others in arguing that, with the realm reunited, the court ought to revive the classical Feng and Shan sacrifices on Mount Tai; they pressed the point in memorial after memorial, but the emperor modestly refused.
value.literal: Shu together with Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Zhang Hua, and others, because the six directions were mixed in one, held it proper to use classical rites to feng and shan at the eastern marchmount; before and after repeatedly they presented this matter; the emperor modestly yielded and did not permit.

value.zh: 以舒為左僕射，領吏部。
value.en: Shu was named left vice-director of the Masters of Writing and placed in charge of the Personnel Ministry.
value.literal: They appointed Shu Left Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, concurrently heading the Personnel Ministry.

value.zh: 舒上言：「今選六宮，聘以玉帛，而舊使禦府丞奉聘，宣成嘉禮，贄重使輕。
value.en: Shu memorialized: "Selection for the six palaces still relies on jade and silk betrothal gifts, yet we continue to send the deputy superintendent of the palace storehouse as envoy—the treasure is weighty while the messenger is slight.
value.literal: Shu submitted words: "Now in selecting the six palaces betrothal uses jade and silk, yet the old practice sends the Palace Storehouse deputy to carry betrothal, proclaiming and completing the fine rite, while the gifts are heavy and the envoy light.

value.zh: 以為拜三夫人宜使卿，九嬪使五官中郎將，美人、良人使謁者，於典制為弘。」
value.en: I propose that investiture of the three senior consorts be entrusted to ministers, the nine imperial concubines to gentlemen of the household for all purposes, and the lower ranks of palace ladies to court heralds—so the ritual weight matches the statutes."
value.literal: I hold that for investing the three great consorts it is proper to use ministers, for the nine concubines to use Gentlemen of the Household for All Purposes, for beauties and chosen ladies to use heralds — toward canonical regulation this is magnified."

value.zh: 有詔詳之，眾議異同，遂寢。
value.en: The court ordered a full discussion, but opinions clashed and the plan was shelved.
value.literal: There was an edict to deliberate it in detail; the crowd's discussions differed in agreement, and therefore it slept.

value.zh: 加右光祿大夫、儀同三司。
value.en: He received the additional titles of grand master of the right and privilege equal to the Three Dukes.
value.literal: He was added Grand Master of the Right with parity of the Three Dukes.

value.zh: 及山濤薨，以舒領司徒，有頃即真。
value.en: When Shan Tao died, Shu was ordered to oversee the ministry of education and soon received full appointment.
value.literal: When Shan Tao died, they ordered Shu to act as Minister of Education; after a little while he received substantive appointment.

value.zh: 舒有威重德望，祿賜散之九族，家無餘財。
value.en: Shu combined moral authority with high prestige; stipends and gifts he shared across his entire kindred, leaving nothing hoarded at home.
value.literal: Shu had awesome weight and virtuous repute; stipends and gifts he scattered among the nine kinships; the household had no surplus wealth.

value.zh: 陳留周震累為諸府所辟，辟書既下，公輒喪亡，僉號震為殺公掾，莫有辟者。
value.en: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu had been summoned again and again, yet each time the appointment was issued his patron died; people called him the adjutant who killed his superiors, and no one would hire him.
value.literal: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu repeatedly was summoned by various bureaus; once the summons letter had descended, the grandee always died; all called Zhen the adjutant who kills lords, and there was none who summoned him.

value.zh: 舒乃命之，而竟無患，識者以此稱其達命。
value.en: Shu summoned him nonetheless, and no misfortune followed; observers praised this as proof of Shu's grasp of fate.
value.literal: Shu then ordered him, and in the end there was no calamity; those who knew praised him on this account as comprehending destiny.

value.zh: 以年老，每稱疾遜位。
value.en: In old age he often pleaded illness in order to resign.
value.literal: Because of old age, he repeatedly claimed illness to yield position.

value.zh: 中復暫起，署兗州中正，尋又稱疾。
value.en: He briefly returned to office as middle appraiser for Yan Province, then again pleaded sickness.
value.literal: In the middle again he briefly rose, was appointed middle appraiser of Yan Province, and presently again claimed illness.

value.zh: 尚書左丞郤詵與舒書曰：「公久疾小差，視事是也，唯上所念。
value.en: Xi Shen, left assistant in the Secretariat, wrote: "You have been ill a long time but are a little better; resuming duty is what the throne expects.
value.literal: Xi Shen, Left Assistant in the Secretariat, wrote Shu a letter, saying, "You have long been ill and slightly improved; attending to affairs is right — it is what those above think of.

value.zh: 何竟起訖還臥，曲身回法，甚失具瞻之望。
value.en: Why rise only to go straight back to bed, bending every rule? You disappoint the court that looks to you for guidance.
value.literal: Why altogether rise and finish and return to bed, bending the body and twisting the law — greatly losing the expectation of being looked up to.

value.zh: 公少立巍巍，一旦棄之，可不惜哉！」
value.en: You built a towering reputation in youth—to throw it away now would be a bitter waste!"
value.literal: You from youth established towering height; in one morning to cast it — can it not be pitied!"

value.zh: 舒稱疾如初。
value.en: Shu pleaded illness as stubbornly as before.
value.literal: Shu claimed illness as at first.

value.zh: 後以災異遜位，帝不聽。
value.en: Later he cited portents and offered to retire, but the emperor would not hear of it.
value.literal: Later because of disasters and anomalies he yielded position; the emperor did not listen.

value.zh: 後因正旦朝罷還第，表送章綬。
value.en: Then, after New Year's court, he went home and submitted his seals and ribbons of office.
value.literal: Later because on New Year's dawn court finished he returned to mansion and memorialized sending seals and ribbons.

value.zh: 帝手詔敦勉。
value.en: The emperor answered with a personal edict urging him to stay.
value.literal: The emperor by hand edict earnestly urged him.

value.zh: 而舒執意彌固，乃下詔曰：「司徒、劇陽子舒，體道弘粹，思量經遠，忠肅居正，在公盡規。
value.en: Shu only dug in harder, so the throne issued an edict: "Minister of Education and Viscount of Ji, Wei Shu, embodies the Way in its pure breadth; his plans look far ahead; he is loyal, grave, and upright, and in office he has never stinted honest counsel.
value.literal: Yet Shu held his intent more firm; then an edict was issued, saying, "Minister of Education, Viscount of Ji, Shu embodies the Way in broad purity, thought and measure reach far, loyal and reverent he holds to the straight, in public he exhausts regulation.

value.zh: 入管銓衡，官人允敘；
value.en: Within the ministry he balanced appointments so that every post went to a fitting man;
value.literal: Within he managed the balance of appointments, ranking officials in suitable order;

value.zh: 出贊袞職，敷弘五教。
value.en: without he aided the highest councils and spread the five teachings of moral order.
value.literal: without he assisted the ducal robe office, spread and enlarged the five teachings.

value.zh: 惠訓播流，德聲茂著，可謂朝之俊乂者也。
value.en: His gentle instruction has spread everywhere and his virtuous name shines bright—he is truly one of the great pillars of the court.
value.literal: Kind instruction spreads and flows; virtuous fame flourishes bright — he may be called the court's outstanding talent.

value.zh: 而屢執沖讓，辭旨懇誠，申覽反覆，省用憮然。
value.en: Yet he presses his modest resignations again and again, and each memorial is so earnest that, reading them back and forth, I must grieve.
value.literal: Yet repeatedly he presses modest yielding; his words' intent is earnest and sincere; extending and viewing back and forth, examining it I am sorrowful.

value.zh: 蓋成人之美，先典所與，難違至情。
value.en: Ancient canons praise those who crown another man's excellence, and I cannot lightly set aside such heartfelt devotion.
value.literal: For crowning others' excellence is what former canons grant; it is hard to reject utmost feeling.

value.zh: 今聽其所執，以劇陽子就第，位同三司，祿賜如前。
value.en: I therefore grant what he asks: he may retire to his mansion as viscount of Ji with rank equal to the Three Dukes and stipends as before.
value.literal: Now I listen to what he insists on: as Viscount of Ji he goes to mansion, rank equal to Three Dukes, stipends and gifts as before.

value.zh: 几杖不朝，賜錢百萬，床帳簟褥自副。
value.en: He need not attend court; he receives a million cash, with bed-curtains, fine mats, and bedding supplied.
value.literal: With folding-stool and staff not attending court; bestowed one million cash; bed curtains, bamboo mats, bedding self-attached.

value.zh: 以舍人四人為劇陽子舍人，置官騎十人。
value.en: Four chamberlains shall attend him as householders of the viscount of Ji, with ten mounted escorts.
value.literal: With four chamberlains as householders to the Viscount of Ji, establish official riders ten men.

value.zh: 使光祿勳奉策，主者詳案典禮，令皆如舊制。」
value.en: Let the master of ceremonies present the rescript, and let the bureaus review the statutes so every detail follows precedent."
value.literal: Cause the Master of Ceremonies to bear the rescript; those in charge shall in detail examine canonical rites, ordering all like old regulations."

value.zh: 於是賜安車駟馬，門施行馬。
value.en: He was then granted a secure carriage and four-horse team, and a mounting-block was set at his gate.
value.literal: Thereupon he was bestowed secure carriage and four-horse team; at the gate was applied riding horse block.

value.zh: 舒為事必先行而後言，遜位之際，莫有知者。
value.en: Shu always acted before he spoke; when he resigned, no one had seen it coming.
value.literal: Shu in doing affairs always first acted and afterward spoke; at the juncture of yielding position, there was none who knew.

value.zh: 時論以為晉興以來，三公能辭榮善終者，未之有也。
value.en: Public opinion held that since the founding of Jin no holder of the three highest posts had refused honor and finished his career with such dignity.
value.literal: Contemporary discussion held that since Jin's rise, among Three Dukes able to decline glory and end well, there had not been such.

value.zh: 司空衛瓘與舒書曰：「每與足下共論此事，日日未果，可謂瞻之在前，忽焉在後矣。」
value.en: Minister of Works Wei Guan wrote him, "We spoke of this again and again yet never settled it—truly it was always 'right before our eyes,' then 'gone in an instant,' as the saying goes."
value.literal: Minister of Works Wei Guan wrote Shu a letter, saying, "Whenever with you I together discussed this matter, day by day not yet fruit — it may be called 'it seemed before the eyes, suddenly afterward."

value.zh: 太熙元年薨，時年八十二。
value.en: He died in the first year of Taixi, aged eighty-two.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi he died; at the time his years were eighty-two.

value.zh: 帝甚傷悼，賵賻優厚，諡曰康。
value.en: The emperor grieved deeply, sent lavish funeral gifts, and gave him the posthumous name Kang, "Peaceful."
value.literal: The emperor greatly mourned; funeral gifts were generous and thick; his posthumous name was Kang.

value.zh: 劉毅
value.en: Liu Yi.
value.literal: Liu Yi.

value.zh: 疏奏，優詔答之。
value.en: The throne answered with a gracious edict.
value.literal: When the memorial was submitted, a gracious edict replied.

value.zh: 後司空衛瓘等亦共表宜省九品，復古鄉議里選。
value.en: Later Wei Guan and others jointly urged cutting nine ranks and reviving village recommendation.
value.literal: Later Minister of Works Wei Guan and others jointly memorialized that one ought to reduce the nine ranks and restore ancient village deliberation and hamlet selection.

value.zh: 帝竟不施行。
value.en: The emperor never acted on it.
value.literal: The Emperor in the end did not implement it.

value.zh: 由是毅遂為州都，銓正人流，清濁區別，其所彈貶，自親貴者始。
value.en: Yi took the provincial seat, sorted candidates, split worthy from worthless, and struck kin and grandees first.
value.literal: By this Yi became provincial rectifier—evaluating and rectifying the human stream—clear and muddy distinguished—those he impeached and demoted began from kin and nobility.

value.zh: 太康六年卒，武帝撫幾驚曰：「失吾名臣，不得生作三公！」
value.en: He died in Taikang 6; Emperor Wu smacked the rail: "We lost a pillar—he never lived to join the Three Dukes!"
value.literal: In the sixth year of Taikang he died; Emperor Wu stroked the armrest and said startled: "We have lost Our famed minister—cannot have him live to serve among the Three Dukes!"

value.zh: 即贈儀同三司，使者監護喪事。
value.en: They granted him parity with the Three Offices with courtiers overseeing his obsequies.
value.literal: Immediately posthumously conferred parity with the Three Offices; envoys supervised the funeral.

value.zh: 羽林左監北海王宮上疏曰：「中詔以毅忠允匪躬，贈班台司，斯誠聖朝考績以毅著勳之美事也。
value.en: Colonel Wang Gong wrote: "The palace honors Yi's loyalty—posthumous Three Offices rank crowns real service.
value.literal: Colonel of the Feathered Forest left guard, Wang Gong of Beihai, submitted a memorial: "The inner edict because Yi was loyal and fair without sparing himself grants Three Offices rank—this is truly the sagely court examining merit for Yi's manifest achievement.

value.zh: 臣謹按，諡者行之跡，而號者功之表。
value.en: Posthumous names record conduct; noble titles record deeds.
value.literal: Your servant respectfully examines—posthumous title is the trace of conduct—while honorific title is the showing of merit.

value.zh: 今毅功德並立，而有號無諡，於義不體。
value.en: Yi earned both virtue and achievement yet lacks a posthumous name—that breaks precedent.
value.literal: Now Yi's merit and virtue both stand—yet he has title without posthumous name—in righteousness not a proper body.

value.zh: 臣竊以《春秋》之事求之，諡法主於行而不系爵。
value.en: The Spring and Autumn ties posthumous names to deeds, not to pedigree.
value.literal: Your servant privately seeks it in Spring and Autumn affairs—posthumous law masters conduct and does not tie to noble rank.

value.zh: 然漢、魏相承，爵非列侯，則皆沒而高行，不加之諡，至使三事之賢臣，不如野戰之將。
value.en: Han and Wei withheld posthumous praise from anyone below full marquis—so loyal ministers ranked beneath battlefield brutes.
value.literal: Yet Han and Wei inherit—if rank is not ranked marquis then all die with high conduct—none adds posthumous title—until worthy ministers of the Three Departments prove less honored than wild campaign generals.

value.zh: 銘跡所殊，臣願聖世舉《春秋》之遠制，改列爵之舊限，使夫功行之實不相掩替，則莫不率賴。
value.en: Your servant asks this court to revive ancient naming rules so merit matches tribute—none would doubt Your fairness.
value.literal: What inscription traces distinguish—your servant wishes the sagely age would raise Spring and Autumn's distant system—alter the old limit of ranked nobility—so that merit and conduct's reality do not obscure each other—then none would fail to depend.

value.zh: 若以革舊毀制，非所倉卒，則毅之忠益，雖不攻城掠地，論德進爵，亦應在例。
value.en: If reform cannot come overnight, Yi's steadfast counsel—though no conqueror—still merits posthumous grace by precedent.
value.literal: If because altering old destroys regulation—not something for haste—then Yi's loyal benefit—even though not storming cities or plundering lands—debating virtue advancing rank—also ought to fall within precedent.

value.zh: 臣敢惟行甫請周之義，謹牒毅功行如石。」
value.en: Following the precedent of humble memorials to Zhou, Your servant lists Yi's deeds below."
value.literal: Your servant dares follow Xingfu's meaning in begging Zhou—respectfully presenting Yi's merit and conduct as stone."

value.zh: 帝出其表使八坐議之，多同宮議。
value.en: The emperor circulated Wang Gong's text to the Eight Seats—most concurred.
value.literal: The Emperor produced his memorial and had the Eight Seats debate—most agreed with Gong's memorial.

value.zh: 奏寢不報。
value.en: The memorial vanished into silence—no answer came.
value.literal: Memorial submitted—slept—no reply.

value.zh: 二子：暾、總。
value.en: He left two sons: Liu Tun and Liu Zong.
value.literal: Two sons: Tun and Zong.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
value.literal: Preface

value.zh: 劉沈，字道真，燕國薊人也。
value.en: Liu Shen, courtesy name Daozhen, came from Ji in Yan.
value.literal: Liu Shen, courtesy name Daozhen, was a man of Ji in the state of Yan.

value.zh: 世為北州名族。
value.en: His clan ranked among the north's great families for generations.
value.literal: For generations his clan was a distinguished house of the northern provinces.

value.zh: 少仕州郡，博學好古。
value.en: Youth brought minor provincial posts; he read widely and revered antiquity.
value.literal: In youth he served in provincial posts; he was broadly learned and loved antiquity.

value.zh: 太保衛瓘辟為掾，領本邑大中正。
value.en: Grand Mentor Wei Guan took him on as an aide and put him in charge of local personnel appraisal as senior rectifier.
value.literal: Grand Mentor Wei Guan summoned him as aide and assigned him concurrent duty as senior rectifier for his native district.

value.zh: 敦儒道，愛賢能，進霍原為二品，及申理張華，皆辭旨明峻，為當時所稱。
value.en: He championed scholarship, prized talent, promoted Huo Yuan to the second grade, and defended Zhang Hua—each memorial lucid and uncompromising, earning wide acclaim.
value.literal: He honored Confucian teaching and loved worthy talent; advancing Huo Yuan to the second rank and arguing Zhang Hua's case—all were marked by bright, stern wording and praised by contemporaries.

value.zh: 齊王冏輔政，引為左長史，遷侍中。
value.en: Prince of Qi Sima Jiong, while directing government, brought Liu Shen in as Left Senior Clerk and soon promoted him to Palace Attendant.
value.literal: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong directed affairs, he summoned Shen as Left Senior Clerk and promoted him to Palace Attendant.

value.zh: 于時李流亂蜀，詔沈以侍中、假節，統益州刺史羅尚、梁州刺史許雄等以討流。
value.en: While Li Liu ravaged Shu, the throne named Liu Shen Palace Attendant with credential staff to coordinate Luo Shang of Yi Province, Xu Xiong of Liang Province, and others against him.
value.literal: At that time Li Liu rebelled in Shu; an edict appointed Shen as Palace Attendant with credential staff to oversee Inspector of Yi Province Luo Shang, Inspector of Liang Province Xu Xiong, and others to strike Liu.

value.zh: 行次長安，河間王顒請留沉為軍司，遣席薳代之。
value.en: His march paused at Chang'an; Prince of Hejian Sima Yong asked to keep Liu Shen as army marshal and dispatched Xi Yuan to replace him on campaign.
value.literal: Marching, he halted at Chang'an; Prince of Hejian Yong requested to retain Shen as army marshal and sent Xi Yuan to replace him.

value.zh: 後領雍州刺史。
value.en: He later added concurrent duty as Inspector of Yong Province.
value.literal: Later he concurrently served as Inspector of Yong Province.

value.zh: 及張昌作亂，詔顒遣沉將州兵萬人並征西府五千人，自藍田關以討之，顒不奉詔。
value.en: When Zhang Chang rose, an edict told Yong to send Liu Shen with ten thousand Yong troops and five thousand western expedition troops through Lantian Pass—Yong ignored it.
value.literal: When Zhang Chang rebelled, an edict ordered Yong to send Shen leading ten thousand provincial troops plus five thousand from the western expedition headquarters through Lantian Pass to attack him; Yong did not obey the edict.

value.zh: 沉自領州兵至藍田，顒又逼奪其眾。
value.en: Liu Shen drove the provincial army to Lantian anyway; Yong seized those troops from him.
value.literal: Shen himself led provincial troops to Lantian; Yong again pressed and seized his forces.

value.zh: 長沙王乂命沉將武吏四百人還州。
value.en: Prince of Changsha Sima Yi ordered Liu Shen to march four hundred armed clerks back to Yong Province.
value.literal: Prince of Changsha Yi ordered Shen to lead four hundred martial clerks back to the province.

value.zh: 宋本紀下第三
value.en: Liu Song Annals, Part Three.
value.literal: Liu Song Annals, lower scroll, third.

value.zh: 帝好讀書，愛文義，在藩時撰江左以來文章志，又續衛瓘所注論語二卷。
value.en: The emperor loved reading and valued literary culture. While still a prince he compiled a record of writings from the lands east of the Yangzi since the Jin, and continued Wei Guan's annotated Lunyu in two scrolls.
value.literal: The emperor loved reading and cherished literary principles; while still in his princedom he compiled a record of writings from the lands east of the Yangzi since the Jin, and also continued Wei Guan's annotated Lunyu in two scrolls.

value.zh: 及即大位，舊臣才學之士多蒙引進。
value.en: Once enthroned, he favored and promoted many veteran ministers and learned men.
value.literal: When he reached the great throne, many old ministers and men of learning were favored and promoted.

value.zh: 末年好鬼神，多忌諱，言語文書有禍敗凶喪疑似之言應回避者，犯即加戮。
value.en: In his later years he grew obsessed with spirits and taboos. Any word in speech or documents suggesting disaster, defeat, or death that ought to be avoided would, if uttered, bring immediate execution.
value.literal: In his later years he favored spirits and ghosts and was full of taboos; in speech and documents, any word suggesting disaster, defeat, mourning, or death that ought to be avoided—if violated, execution followed at once.

value.zh: 改「騧」馬字為「馬」邊「瓜」，以「騧」字似「禍」故也。
value.en: He changed the character for "piebald horse" to "horse" beside "melon," because the original character resembled the character for "disaster."
value.literal: He changed the character for "piebald horse" to "horse" beside "melon," because the character for "piebald horse" resembled the character for "disaster."

value.zh: 嘗以南苑借張永，云：「且給三百年，期盡更請。」
value.en: He once lent the Southern Park to Zhang Yong, saying, "I shall lend it for three hundred years; when the term expires you may ask again."
value.literal: He once lent the Southern Park to Zhang Yong, saying: "I shall lend it for three hundred years; when the term expires you may ask again."

value.zh: 宣陽門謂之白門，上以白門不祥，諱之。
value.en: The Xuanyang Gate was called the White Gate; the emperor considered "white gate" inauspicious and forbade the name.
value.literal: The Xuanyang Gate was called the White Gate; the sovereign considered "white gate" inauspicious and tabooed it.

value.zh: 尚書右丞江謐嘗誤犯，上變色曰：「白汝家門！」
value.en: Jiang Mi, Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, once accidentally violated the taboo. The emperor flushed and said, "May whiteness fall upon your family's gate!"
value.literal: Jiang Mi, Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, once accidentally violated the taboo; the sovereign changed color and said: "White upon your family's gate!"

value.zh: 路太后停屍漆床移出東宮，上幸宮見之，怒，免中庶子，以之坐死者數十人。
value.en: When Empress Dowager Lu's corpse was moved out of the Eastern Palace on a lacquered couch, the emperor visited the palace, saw it, flew into a rage, dismissed the Palace Mentor, and several dozen men were put to death on that account.
value.literal: When Empress Dowager Lu's corpse was moved out of the Eastern Palace on a lacquered couch, the sovereign visited the palace, saw it, grew angry, dismissed the Palace Mentor, and several dozen men were put to death on that account.

value.zh: 內外常慮犯觸，人不自保。
value.en: Within and without the court, everyone lived in constant fear of giving offense and could not protect themselves.
value.literal: Within and without, people constantly feared giving offense and could not protect themselves.

value.zh: 移床修壁，先祭土神，使文士為祝策，如大祭饗。
value.en: Before moving beds or repairing walls, they first sacrificed to the earth god and had literary men compose prayer texts as at a great sacrificial feast.
value.literal: When moving beds or repairing walls, they first sacrificed to the earth god and had literary men compose prayer texts, as at a great sacrificial feast.

value.zh: 霍峻字仲邈，南郡枝江人也。
value.en: Huo Jun, styled Zhongmiao, came from Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.
value.literal: Huo Jun, courtesy name Zhongmiao, was a man of Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.

value.zh: 兄篤於鄉里合部曲數百人，篤卒，荊州牧劉表令峻攝其眾。
value.en: His older brother Huo Du had raised a few hundred local followers; after Du died, Jing governor Liu Biao put Jun in charge of that band.
value.literal: His elder brother Huo Du in the countryside assembled several hundred retainers in a private corps; when Du died, the Governor of Jing Province, Liu Biao, ordered Jun to take command of his troops.

value.zh: 表卒，峻率眾歸先主，先主以峻為中郎將。
value.en: After Liu Biao’s death, Jun brought his men to Liu Bei, who made him a general of the household.
value.literal: When Liu Biao died, Jun led the troops to submit to the First Sovereign, who appointed Jun General of the Gentlemen of the Household.

value.zh: 先主自葭萌南還襲劉璋，留峻守葭萌城。
value.en: Liu Bei marched south from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang and left Huo Jun to hold the fortress there.
value.literal: The First Sovereign returned south from Jiameng to strike Liu Zhang, leaving Jun to defend Jiameng city.

value.zh: 張魯遣將楊帛誘峻，求共守城，峻曰：「小人頭可得，城不可得。」
value.en: Zhang Lu’s officer Yang Bo tried to win him over for a joint defense, but Huo Jun replied, "You may have my head; you will not have this city."
value.literal: Zhang Lu sent the general Yang Bo to entice Jun, seeking to defend the city together; Jun said, "This petty man's head may be taken, but the city cannot be taken."

value.zh: 帛乃退去。
value.en: Yang Bo withdrew his force.
value.literal: Bo thereupon withdrew.

value.zh: 後璋將扶禁、向存等帥萬餘人由閬水上，攻圍攻峻，且一年，不能下。
value.en: Liu Zhang’s generals Fu Jin and Xiang Cun then brought over ten thousand men up the Lang River and besieged the town for the better part of a year without breaking it.
value.literal: Later Zhang's generals Fu Jin, Xiang Cun, and others led more than ten thousand men up the Lang River, attacked, besieged, and assaulted Jun for nearly a year but could not take him.

value.zh: 峻城中兵才數百人，伺其怠隙，選精銳出擊，大破之，即斬存首。
value.en: Huo Jun had only a few hundred defenders. When he saw an opening, he sent picked troops out in a sortie, routed the besiegers, and took Xiang Cun’s head.
value.literal: Jun had only several hundred soldiers in the city; watching for their slackness and gaps, he selected crack troops, sallied out, struck them a great defeat, and beheaded Cun on the spot.

value.zh: 先主定蜀，嘉峻之功，乃分廣漢為梓潼郡，以峻為梓潼太守、裨將軍。
value.en: Once Liu Bei had secured Shu, he singled out Huo Jun’s exploit, carved Zitong commandery out of Guanghan, and named him its governor with the rank of major general.
value.literal: The First Sovereign settled Shu, praised Jun's merit, thereupon divided Guanghan to make Zitong Commandery, and appointed Jun Administrator of Zitong and Major General.

value.zh: 在官三年，年四十卒，還葬成都。
value.en: He served three years in post, died at forty, and was brought home for burial in Chengdu.
value.literal: In office three years, at age forty he died; he was returned for burial at Chengdu.

value.zh: 先主甚悼惜，乃詔諸葛亮曰：「峻既佳士，加有功於國，欲行爵。」
value.en: The First Sovereign mourned him deeply and issued an edict to Zhuge Liang: "Jun was an excellent man and, moreover, had rendered merit to the state. I wish to grant him rank."
value.literal: The First Sovereign greatly mourned and pitied him, then issued an edict to Zhuge Liang saying, "Jun is already an excellent gentleman, moreover having merit for the state; I wish to carry out enfeoffment."

value.zh: 遂親率群僚臨會弔祭，因留宿墓上，當時榮之。
value.en: He then led the full court to the funeral, stayed the night by the grave, and contemporaries counted it the highest honor.
value.literal: Thereupon he personally led the host of officials to attend the assembly, mourn, and sacrifice, and on that account lodged overnight on the tomb; at the time they deemed it glorious.

value.zh: 朗兄子寵，先主時為牙門將。
value.en: Xiang Lang's elder brother's son Xiang Chong served as general of the household yamen under the Former Lord.
value.literal: Lang's elder brother's son Chong, in the Former Lord's time served as general of the household yamen.

value.zh: 秭歸之敗，寵營特完。
value.en: At the defeat at Zigui, Chong's camp alone remained intact.
value.literal: At the defeat at Zigui, Chong's camp alone remained intact.

value.zh: 建興元年223年封都亭侯，後為中部督，典宿衛兵。
value.en: In Jianxing 1 (223) he was enfeoffed marquis of Duting; later he became supervisor of the central section and commanded the palace guard.
value.literal: In the first year of Jianxing, 223, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Duting; later he became supervisor of the central section and directed the palace guard.

value.zh: 諸葛亮當北行，表與後主曰：「將軍向寵，性行淑均，曉暢軍事，試用於昔，先帝稱之曰能，是以眾論舉寵為督。
value.en: When Zhuge Liang was about to march north, he memorialized the emperor: "General Xiang Chong is even-tempered and fair, and well versed in military affairs. The late emperor tested him in earlier days and praised his ability, and the court therefore recommended him as camp supervisor.
value.literal: When Zhuge Liang was about to march north, he memorialized the Later Lord, saying: "General Xiang Chong is even and fair in nature and conduct, well versed in military affairs; tested in former days, the late Emperor praised him as capable, and so by common counsel Chong was recommended as supervisor.

value.zh: 愚以為營中之事，悉以咨之，必能使行陳和睦，優劣得所也。」
value.en: I believe that in camp affairs, if you consult him on everything, the ranks will stay harmonious and each man will be placed according to his worth."
value.literal: Your servant thinks that in camp affairs, if you consult him on all, you will surely make the ranks harmonious and assign merit and fault to their proper places."

value.zh: 遷中領軍。
value.en: He was promoted to director of the central army.
value.literal: He was transferred to director of the central army.

value.zh: 延熙三年，征漢嘉蠻夷，遇害。
value.en: In Yanxi 3 (240) he campaigned against the Hanjia tribes and was killed.
value.literal: In the third year of Yanxi he campaigned against the Hanjia barbarians and met with harm.

value.zh: 寵弟充，歷射聲校尉、尚書。
value.en: Chong's younger brother Xiang Chong served as colonel of the army of loud-shouting archers and as master of writing.
value.literal: Chong's younger brother Chong served as colonel of the army of loud-shouting archers and as master of writing.

value.zh: 《襄阳记》曰：魏咸熙元年六月，镇西将军卫瓘至於成都，得璧玉印各一枚，文似“成信”字，魏人宣示百官，藏于相国府。
value.en: The Xiangyang ji records that in the sixth month of Wei Xianxi 1 (264), General Who Guards the West Wei Guan reached Chengdu and found a pair of jade seals inscribed with characters resembling "completed faith"; Wei officials displayed them to the court and stored them in the chancellor's mansion.
value.literal: The Xiangyang ji states: In the sixth month of the first year of Xianxi in Wei, General Who Guards the West Wei Guan reached Chengdu and obtained one jade seal each, the inscription resembling the characters for "completed faith"; the men of Wei displayed them to the hundred officials and stored them in the chancellor's mansion.

value.zh: 充闻之曰：“吾闻谯周之言，先帝讳备，其训具也，后主讳禅，其训授也，如言刘已具矣，当授与人也。
value.en: Xiang Chong said: "I have heard Qiao Zhou's remark—the Former Lord's taboo name Bei means 'complete,' and the Later Lord's taboo name Shan means 'hand over,' as though the Liu house were finished and due to be handed on.
value.literal: Chong heard of it and said: "I have heard Qiao Zhou's words: the Former Lord's taboo name Bei, its gloss is 'complete'; the Later Lord's taboo name Shan, its gloss is 'hand over'; as if saying the Liu house is already complete and should be handed to another.

value.zh: 今中抚军名炎，而汉年极於炎兴，瑞出成都，而藏之於相国府，此殆天意也。”
value.en: Now the Central Pacifier is named Yan, Han's years end in Yanxing, the omen appeared at Chengdu and was stored in the chancellor's mansion—surely this is heaven's intent."
value.literal: Now the Central Pacifier is named Yan, and the Han years end in Yanxing; the omen appeared at Chengdu yet is stored in the chancellor's mansion—this is perhaps heaven's intent.

value.zh: 是岁，拜充为梓潼太守，明年十二月而晋武帝即尊位，炎兴於是乎徵焉。
value.en: That year Xiang Chong was appointed governor of Zitong; in the twelfth month of the next year Emperor Wu of Jin took the throne, and Yanxing was thereby fulfilled.
value.literal: That year Chong was appointed Administrator of Zitong; in the twelfth month of the next year Emperor Wu of Jin assumed the exalted position, and Yanxing was thereby fulfilled.

value.zh: 孙盛曰：昔公孙自以起成都，号曰成氏，二玉之文，殆述所作乎！
value.en: Sun Sheng said: When Gongsun Shu rose from Chengdu and styled himself the Cheng clan, the inscription on the two jades perhaps described what he had done!
value.literal: Sun Sheng said: Formerly Gongsun [Sun] took Chengdu as his rise and styled himself the Cheng clan—the text on the two jades perhaps describes what he wrought!

value.zh: 志第十三 天文一
value.en: Treatise Thirteen: Astronomy, Part One
value.literal: Treatise 13: Astronomy 1

value.zh: 泰始十年十二月，有星孛於軫。
value.en: the tenth year of Taishi, twelfth month: a comet appeared in Chariot Shaft.
value.literal: Taishi year 10, twelfth month: a broom star appeared at Chariot Shaft.

value.zh: 占曰：「天下兵起。
value.en: Prognostication reads: "War will erupt across the empire.
value.literal: Prognostication says: "Warfare rises throughout the realm.

value.zh: 軫又楚分也。」
value.en: Chariot Shaft also marks Chu's domain."
value.literal: Chariot Shaft is also Chu's allotted field."

value.zh: 咸寧二年六月，星孛於氐。
value.en: In Xianning 2, sixth month, a comet appeared at Root.
value.literal: Xianning year 2, sixth month: a broom star appeared at Root.

value.zh: 占曰：「天子失德易政。
value.en: Prognostication reads: "The sovereign forfeits virtue and the throne changes hands.
value.literal: Prognostication says: "The Son of Heaven loses virtue and the regime changes.

value.zh: 氐又兗州分。」
value.en: Root also marks Yanzhou's domain."
value.literal: Root is also Yanzhou's allotted field."

value.zh: 七月，星孛大角。
value.en: In the seventh month a comet appeared at Great Horn.
value.literal: Seventh month: a broom star appeared at Great Horn.

value.zh: 大角為帝坐。
value.en: Great Horn is the throne star of the sovereign.
value.literal: Great Horn is the Emperor's Seat.

value.zh: 八月，星孛太微，至翼、北斗、三台。
value.en: In the eighth month a comet appeared in Supreme Subtlety and passed through Wings, the Northern Dipper, and the Three Steps.
value.literal: Eighth month: a broom star appeared at Supreme Subtlety, reaching Wings, Northern Dipper, and Three Steps.

value.zh: 占曰：「太微天子廷，大人惡之。」
value.en: Prognostication reads: "Supreme Subtlety is the imperial court—great men will suffer for it."
value.literal: Prognostication says: "Supreme Subtlety is the Son of Heaven's court; great men dread it."

value.zh: 一曰：「有徙王。
value.en: Another reading says: "A deposed prince will be moved.
value.literal: One account says: "There will be a transferred king.

value.zh: 翼又楚分也。」
value.en: Wings also marks Chu's domain."
value.literal: Wings is also Chu's allotted field."

value.zh: 「北斗主殺罰，三台為三公。」
value.en: "The Northern Dipper presides over execution and judgment; the Three Steps represent the Three Dukes."
value.literal: "Northern Dipper governs killing and punishment; Three Steps are the Three Dukes."

value.zh: 三年，星孛於胃。
value.en: In Xianning 3 a comet appeared at Stomach.
value.literal: Year 3: a broom star appeared at Stomach.

value.zh: 胃，徐州分。
value.en: Stomach marks Xuzhou's domain.
value.literal: Stomach is Xuzhou's allotted field.

value.zh: 四月，星孛女御。
value.en: In the fourth month a comet appeared at Female Charioteer.
value.literal: Fourth month: a broom star appeared at Female Charioteer.

value.zh: 女御為後宮。
value.en: Female Charioteer governs the inner harem.
value.literal: Female Charioteer is the rear palace.

value.zh: 五月，又孛於東方。
value.en: In the fifth month another comet appeared in the east.
value.literal: Fifth month: a broom star again appeared in the east.

value.zh: 七月，星孛紫宮。
value.en: In the seventh month a comet appeared in Purple Palace.
value.literal: Seventh month: a broom star appeared at Purple Palace.

value.zh: 占曰：「天下易主。」
value.en: Prognostication reads: "The empire will change hands."
value.literal: Prognostication says: "The realm changes its ruler."

value.zh: 五年三月，星孛于柳。
value.en: In Xianning 5, third month, a comet appeared at Willow.
value.literal: Year 5, third month: a broom star appeared at Willow.

value.zh: 占曰：「外臣陵主。
value.en: Prognostication reads: "Outer vassals will overpower their lord.
value.literal: Prognostication says: "Outer ministers encroach upon the ruler.

value.zh: 柳又三河分也。
value.en: Willow also marks the Three Rivers domain.
value.literal: Willow is also the Three Rivers' allotted field.

value.zh: 大角、太微、紫宮、女御，並為王者。」
value.en: Great Horn, Supreme Subtlety, Purple Palace, and Female Charioteer all stand for royal power."
value.literal: Great Horn, Supreme Subtlety, Purple Palace, and Female Charioteer all represent the kingly ruler."

value.zh: 明年吳亡，是其應也。
value.en: The following year Wu fell—the omen fulfilled.
value.literal: The next year Wu perished—this was its fulfillment.

value.zh: 孛主兵喪，征吳之役，三河、徐、兗之兵悉出，交戰于吳、楚之地。
value.en: Comets presage war and death; in the conquest of Wu, forces from the Three Rivers, Xu, and Yan all took the field and clashed in the Wu-Chu heartland.
value.literal: Broom stars govern warfare and mourning; in the campaign against Wu, armies of the Three Rivers, Xu, and Yan all marched out and joined battle in Wu and Chu territory.

value.zh: 吳丞相都督以下，梟戮十數，偏裨行陣之徒，馘斬萬計，皆其征也。
value.en: More than a dozen Wu chancellors and commanders were executed and exposed; lieutenants and common soldiers fell by the tens of thousands—all of it the comet's doing.
value.literal: Among Wu, from chancellors and area commanders downward, more than ten were decapitated and displayed; among lieutenants and rank-and-file in the battle lines, those beheaded and killed numbered in the tens of thousands—all signs of it.

value.zh: 《春秋》星孛北方，則齊、魯、晉、鄭、陳、宋、莒之君，並受殺亂之禍。
value.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals record that when a comet appeared in the north, the rulers of Qi, Lu, Jin, Zheng, Chen, Song, and Ju all met violent ruin.
value.literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a broom star appeared in the north, the rulers of Qi, Lu, Jin, Zheng, Chen, Song, and Ju all suffered the calamity of slaughter and disorder.

value.zh: 星孛東方，則楚滅陳，三家、田氏分篡齊、晉。
value.en: An eastern comet foretold Chu destroying Chen and the great houses of Jin and Qi carving up their states.
value.literal: When a broom star appeared in the east, Chu destroyed Chen, and the Three Families and the Tian clan partitioned and usurped Qi and Jin.

value.zh: 漢文帝末，星孛西方，後吳、楚七國誅滅。
value.en: Near the end of Emperor Wen's reign a comet appeared in the west; soon after the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu were crushed.
value.literal: At the end of Emperor Wen of Han, a broom star appeared in the west; afterward the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu were exterminated.

value.zh: 案泰始末至太康初，災異數見，而晉氏隆盛，吳實滅，天變在吳可知矣。
value.en: From late Taishi through early Taikang, omens multiplied even as Jin rose and Wu fell—clear proof that heaven's warnings were aimed at Wu, not Jin.
value.literal: Examined: from the end of Taishi to the beginning of Taikang, calamities and anomalies appeared repeatedly, yet the Jin clan flourished and Wu was truly destroyed—heaven's changes targeted Wu, as can be known.

value.zh: 昔漢三年，星孛大角，項籍以亡，漢氏無事，此項氏主命故也。
value.en: In Han year 3 a comet struck Great Horn: Xiang Yu fell while the Han house stood untouched, for Great Horn governed Xiang's fate.
value.literal: Formerly in Han year 3, a comet baleful at Great Horn—Xiang Yu perished thereby while the Han house was unharmed; this was because Great Horn was the star of Xiang's mandate.

value.zh: 吳、晉之時，天下橫分，大角孛而吳亡，是與項氏同事。
value.en: When Wu and Jin divided the realm, a comet at Great Horn preceded Wu's fall—the same pattern as Xiang Yu's doom.
value.literal: In the age of Wu and Jin, the realm was split across; Great Horn was baleful and Wu perished—this is the same affair as the Xiang clan.

value.zh: 後學皆以咸甯災為晉室，非也。
value.en: Later scholars misread the Xianning omens as warnings to Jin; they are mistaken.
value.literal: Later scholars all take the Xianning calamities as aimed at the Jin house—this is wrong.

value.zh: 晉武帝咸寧四年四月，蚩尤旗見。
value.en: Emperor Wu of Jin, Xianning 4, fourth month: the Chiyou Banner appeared.
value.literal: Jin Emperor Wu, Xianning year 4, fourth month: the Chiyou Banner appeared.

value.zh: 案星傳，蚩尤旗類彗，而後曲象旗。
value.en: Star lore holds that the Chiyou Banner resembles a comet but curves backward like a banner.
value.literal: Examining star lore: the Chiyou Banner resembles a comet, but curves backward like a banner.

value.zh: 漢武帝時見，長竟天。
value.en: Under Emperor Wu of Han it appeared, spanning the entire sky.
value.literal: Under Emperor Wu of Han it appeared, stretching across the whole sky.

value.zh: 獻帝時又見，長十餘丈，皆長星也。
value.en: Under Emperor Xian it appeared again, more than ten zhang long—both were long stars.
value.literal: Under Emperor Xian it appeared again, more than ten zhang long—all were long stars.

value.zh: 魏高貴時則為白氣。
value.en: In Wei's Gaogui era it appeared as white vapor.
value.literal: In the Gaogui era of Wei it was a white vapor.

value.zh: 案校眾記，是歲無長星，宜又是異氣。
value.en: Collating many records shows no long star that year; it was again an anomalous vapor.
value.literal: Examining and collating many records, that year had no long star; it should again have been an anomalous vapor.

value.zh: 後二年，傾三方伐吳，是其應。
value.en: Two years later Jin mobilized on three fronts against Wu—the omen fulfilled.
value.literal: Two years later the three fronts poured forth to attack Wu—this was its fulfillment.

value.zh: 至武帝崩，天下兵又起，遂亡諸夏。
value.en: By Emperor Wu's death war broke out again and the Central States fell into chaos.
value.literal: By the time Emperor Wu died, warfare rose again under Heaven, and the Central States perished.

value.zh: 咸寧四年九月，太白當見不見。
value.en: Xianning 4, ninth month: Venus should have appeared but did not.
value.literal: Xianning year 4, ninth month: Great White should have appeared but did not.

value.zh: 占曰：「是謂失舍，不有破軍，必有死王之墓。
value.en: Prognostication reads: "This is called losing one's station; if no army is shattered, a royal tomb will be opened.
value.literal: Prognostication says: "This is called losing one's lodging; if there is no shattered army, there must be the tomb of a dead king.

value.zh: 又有亡國。」
value.en: A state may also perish."
value.literal: Moreover there is loss of state."

value.zh: 是時羊祜表求伐吳，上許之。
value.en: At that time Yang Hu memorialized to attack Wu and the throne approved.
value.literal: " At that time Yang Hu memorialized requesting an attack on Wu, and the throne approved.

value.zh: 五年十一月，兵出，太白始夕見西方。
value.en: In the fifth year, in the eleventh month, the army marched and Venus first appeared at dusk in the west.
value.literal: In the fifth year, in the eleventh month, the army marched out, and Great White first appeared at dusk in the west.

value.zh: 太康元年三月，大破吳軍，孫晧面縛請死，吳國遂亡。
value.en: Taikang 1, third month: Wu's army was crushed; Sun Hao bound himself and begged for death; Wu fell.
value.literal: Taikang year 1, third month: Wu's army was greatly defeated; Sun Hao bound himself and begged for death; the state of Wu perished.

value.zh: 晉武帝太康二年八月，有星孛于張。
value.en: Emperor Wu of Jin, Taikang 2, eighth month: a comet appeared at Spread.
value.literal: Jin Emperor Wu, Taikang year 2, eighth month: a broom star appeared at Spread.

value.zh: 占曰：「為兵喪。」
value.en: Prognostication reads: "War and mourning follow".
value.literal: Prognostication says: "It presages warfare and mourning".

value.zh: 周分野，災在洛邑。
value.en: Zhou's domain—the calamity struck Luoyang.
value.literal: " Zhou's allotted field—the calamity falls on Luoyang.

value.zh: 十一月，星孛軒轅。
value.en: Eleventh month: a comet appeared at Chariot Shaft.
value.literal: Eleventh month: a broom star baleful at Chariot Shaft.

value.zh: 占曰：「後宮當之。」
value.en: Prognostication reads: "The inner palace will be struck".
value.literal: Prognostication says: "The rear palace is struck".

value.zh: 四年三月戊申，星孛于西南。
value.en: In the fourth year, in the third month, on wushen day, a comet appeared in the southwest.
value.literal: In the fourth year, in the third month, on wushen day, a broom star appeared in the southwest.

value.zh: 四年三月癸丑，齊王攸薨。
value.en: In the fourth year, in the third month, on guichou day, Prince Sima You of Qi died.
value.literal: In the fourth year, in the third month, on guichou day, Prince You of Qi died.

value.zh: 四月戊寅，任城王陵薨。
value.en: Fourth month, day wuyin: Prince of Rencheng Ling died.
value.literal: Fourth month, day wuyin: Prince of Rencheng Ling died.

value.zh: 五月己亥，琅邪王伷薨。
value.en: Fifth month, day jihai: Prince of Langye Xiu died.
value.literal: Fifth month, day jihai: Prince of Langye Xiu died.

value.zh: 十一月戊午，新都王該薨。
value.en: Eleventh month, day wuwu: Prince of Xindu Gai died.
value.literal: Eleventh month, day wuwu: Prince of Xindu Gai died.

value.zh: 太康八年三月，熒惑守心。
value.en: Taikang 8, third month: Mars held station in Heart.
value.literal: Taikang year 8, third month: Sparkling Deluder guarded Heart.

value.zh: 占曰：「王者惡之。」
value.en: Prognostication reads: "The sovereign faces ill omen".
value.literal: Prognostication says: "The kingly ruler is ill-omened".

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: Taixi 1, fourth month, day jiyou: Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: " Taixi year 1, fourth month, day jiyou: Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 太康八年九月，星孛于南斗，長數十丈，十餘日滅。
value.en: Taikang 8, ninth month: a comet tens of zhang long appeared at Southern Dipper and vanished after more than ten days.
value.literal: Taikang year 8, ninth month: a broom star appeared at Southern Dipper, several tens of zhang long; it vanished after more than ten days.

value.zh: 占曰：「斗主爵祿，國有大憂。」
value.en: Prognostication reads: "The Dipper governs rank and salary; the state faces grave danger".
value.literal: Prognostication says: "The Dipper governs rank and stipend; the state has great anxiety".

value.zh: 一曰：「孛于斗，王者疾病，臣誅其父，天下易政，大亂兵起。」
value.en: Alternatively: "A comet at the Dipper means royal illness, a minister kills his father, the realm changes hands, and great war erupts".
value.literal: " One reading says: "A broom star at the Dipper means the kingly ruler falls ill, a minister executes his father, rule changes under Heaven, and great disorder and warfare rise.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月，客星在紫宮。
value.en: Taixi 1, fourth month: a guest star stood in Purple Palace.
value.literal: " Taixi year 1, fourth month: a guest star was in Purple Palace.

value.zh: 占曰：「為兵喪。」
value.en: Prognostication reads: "War and mourning follow".
value.literal: Prognostication says: "It presages warfare and mourning".

value.zh: 太康末，武帝耽宴遊，多疾病。
value.en: Near the end of Taikang Emperor Wu indulged in feasts and tours and grew seriously ill.
value.literal: " At the end of Taikang Emperor Wu indulged in feasting and travel and suffered many illnesses.

value.zh: 是月己酉，帝崩。
value.en: That month, day jiyou: the emperor died.
value.literal: That month, day jiyou: the emperor died.

value.zh: 永平元年，賈后誅楊駿及其黨與，皆夷三族。
value.en: Yongping 1: Empress Jia executed Yang Jun and his faction, destroying all three clans.
value.literal: Yongping year 1: Empress Jia executed Yang Jun and his faction, exterminating all three clans.

value.zh: 楊太后亦見殺。
value.en: Empress Dowager Yang was also killed.
value.literal: Empress Dowager Yang was also killed.

value.zh: 是年，又誅汝南王亮、太保衞瓘、楚王瑋，王室兵喪之應。
value.en: That year Prince of Runan Liang, Grand Tutor Wei Guan, and Prince of Chu Wei were also executed—fulfillment of the royal house's war and mourning.
value.literal: That year Prince of Runan Liang, Grand Tutor Wei Guan, and Prince of Chu Wei were also executed—the royal house's fulfillment of warfare and mourning.

value.zh: 晉惠帝永熙初，衛瓘家人炊飯，墮地，盡化為螺，出足起行。
value.en: Early in Yongxi, rice in Wei Guan's kitchen fell to the floor and turned into snails that sprouted feet and crawled away.
value.literal: In the early Yongxi era of Emperor Hui of Jin, in the household of Wei Guan when cooking rice it fell to the ground and all turned into snails that put out feet, rose, and walked.

value.zh: 螺，龜類，近龜孽也。
value.en: Snails belong to the tortoise family and count as near tortoise omens.
value.literal: Snails are of the tortoise kind and are near to tortoise portents.

value.zh: 干寶曰：「螺被甲，兵象也。
value.en: Gan Bao said: "Snails wear armor—the sign of war.
value.literal: Gan Bao said: "Snails wear armor—the image of arms.

value.zh: 於周易為離，離為戈兵。」
value.en: In the Book of Changes this is Li, the trigram of weapons."
value.literal: In the Book of Changes this is Li, and Li is spear and weapon."

value.zh: 明年，瓘誅。
value.en: The next year Guan was executed.
value.literal: The next year Guan was executed.

value.zh: 十年四月癸丑，崇賢殿災。
value.en: On the guichou day of the fourth month of the tenth year fire destroyed the Chongxian Hall.
value.literal: On the guichou day of the fourth month of the tenth year, the Chongxian Hall burned.

value.zh: 十月庚辰，含章鞠室、脩成堂前廡、丙坊東屋、煇章殿南閣火。
value.en: On the gengchen day of the tenth month fire broke out in the Hanzhang kickball court, the front veranda of the Xiucheng Hall, the eastern rooms of the Bing Ward, and the southern wing of the Huizhang Hall.
value.literal: On the gengchen day of the tenth month, fire struck the Hanzhang cuju court, the front colonnade of the Xiucheng Hall, the eastern rooms of the Bing Ward, and the southern gallery of the Huizhang Hall.

value.zh: 時有上書者曰：「漢王氏五侯兄弟迭任，今楊氏三公並在大位。
value.en: A memorialist wrote at the time, "Under Han the five Wang marquises held office in turn; now the three Yang dukes all stand at the summit of power together.
value.literal: At the time a memorialist said: "Under Han the five marquises of the Wang clan held office in succession as brothers; now the three dukes of the Yang clan all hold high position together.

value.zh: 天變屢見，竊為陛下憂之。」
value.en: Heavenly omens keep appearing, and I cannot help fearing for Your Majesty."
value.literal: Heavenly changes appear repeatedly; I venture to be anxious on Your Majesty's behalf."

value.zh: 楊珧由是乞退。
value.en: Yang Yao thereupon asked to withdraw from office.
value.literal: Yang Yao therefore requested to retire.

value.zh: 是時帝納馮紞之間，廢張華之功；
value.en: At that time the emperor heeded Feng Dan's private advice and cast aside Zhang Hua's merits;
value.literal: At that time the emperor accepted Feng Dan's private counsel and set aside Zhang Hua's achievements;

value.zh: 聽楊駿之讒，離衞瓘之寵。
value.en: listened to Yang Jun's slanders and turned away from Wei Guan's favor.
value.literal: heeded Yang Jun's slanders and estranged himself from Wei Guan's favor.

value.zh: 此逐功臣之罰也。
value.en: This was the retribution for driving out worthy ministers.
value.literal: This was the penalty for expelling meritorious ministers.

value.zh: 明年，宮車晏駕。
value.en: The following year the emperor died.
value.literal: The next year the imperial carriage halted at dusk.

value.zh: 其後楚王承竊發之旨，戮害二公，身亦不免。
value.en: Later the Prince of Chu, acting on a clandestine order, killed the two chief ministers, yet could not save himself.
value.literal: Afterward the Prince of Chu, acting on a secretly issued directive, slaughtered the two grandees, yet he himself did not escape punishment.

value.zh: 震災其坊，又天意乎。
value.en: Lightning had already struck his residence—was that not Heaven's intent as well?
value.literal: Lightning had struck his ward—was this again Heaven's intent?

value.zh: 列傳第二十 范泰王淮之王韶之荀伯子
value.en: Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Zhunzhi, Wang Shaozhi, and Xun Bozi
value.literal: Biographies 20: Fan Tai, Wang Huaizhi, Wang Shaozhi, Xun Bozi

value.zh: 義熙九年，上表曰：「臣聞咎繇亡後，臧文以為深歎；
value.en: In the ninth year of Yixi he submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that after Gao Yao perished, Zang Wen lamented deeply;
value.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi he submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that after Gao Yao perished, Zang Wen deeply lamented;

value.zh: 伯氏奪邑，管仲所以稱仁。
value.en: when the Bo clan lost its fief, Guan Zhong therefore praised the act as humane.
value.literal: when the Bo clan lost its fief, Guan Zhong therefore praised its humanity.

value.zh: 功高可百世不泯，濫賞無崇朝宜許。
value.en: Merit so high may endure for a hundred generations; reckless reward should not be permitted even for a single morning.
value.literal: Merit so high may be unextinguished for a hundred generations; reckless reward should not be permitted even for a single morning.

value.zh: 故太傅鉅平侯祜，明德通賢，宗臣莫二，勳參佐命，功成平吳，而後嗣闕然，烝嘗莫寄。
value.en: The late Grand Tutor, Marquis Juping Hu, combined bright virtue with penetrating worth and stood second to none among the eminent ministers; his merit joined in assisting the Mandate, and when the work of pacifying Wu was done, still his later line was cut off and no one offered the seasonal sacrifices.
value.literal: Thus the late Grand Tutor, Marquis Juping Huo, was of bright virtue and penetrating worth, second to none among the imperial clans; his merit joined in assisting the Mandate, and when the work of pacifying Wu was accomplished, yet his later descendants were cut off and no one offered the seasonal sacrifices.

value.zh: 漢以蕭何元功，故絕世輒紹。
value.en: Because of Xiao He's founding merit, Han whenever the line ended always continued the succession.
value.literal: Han, because of Xiao He's founding merit, whenever the line ended always continued the succession.

value.zh: 愚謂鉅平之封，宜同酇國。
value.en: I humbly believe the enfeoffment of Juping should be treated like the state of Zan.
value.literal: I humbly think the enfeoffment of Juping should be the same as the state of Zan.

value.zh: 故太尉廣陵公陳淮，黨翼孫秀，禍加淮南，竊饗大國，因罪為利。
value.en: The late Grand Marshal, Duke of Guangling Chen Huai, aided and sheltered Sun Xiu; when disaster struck Huainan he usurped enjoyment of a great state and turned crime into profit.
value.literal: The late Grand Marshal, Duke of Guangling Chen Huai, aided and sheltered Sun Xiu; disaster fell on Huainan; he usurped enjoyment of a great state and turned crime into profit.

value.zh: 值西朝政刑失裁，中興復因而不奪。
value.en: It happened that the Western Court lost proper measure in government and punishments, and at the restoration they again followed precedent without revoking the grant.
value.literal: It happened that the Western Court's government and punishments lost proper measure, and at the restoration they again followed precedent and did not revoke it.

value.zh: 今王道惟新，豈可不大判臧否？
value.en: Now that the royal way is newly renewed, how can one fail to judge good and ill on a grand scale?
value.literal: Now the royal way is newly renewed—how can one not greatly distinguish good from ill?

value.zh: 謂廣陵之國，宜在削除。
value.en: I believe the state of Guangling ought to be abolished.
value.literal: I hold that the state of Guangling should be abolished.
