value.zh: 故太保衛瓘，本爵蕭陽縣公，既被橫禍，及進弟秩，始贈蘭陵，又轉江夏。
value.en: The late Grand Guardian Wei Guan had originally held the enfeoffment of Duke of Xiaoyang County; after he suffered violent death, when his younger brother's rank was advanced he was first posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling and then transferred to Jiangxia.
value.literal: The late Grand Guardian Wei Guan originally held the enfeoffment of Duke of Xiaoyang County; having suffered violent death, when his younger brother's rank was advanced he was first posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lanling, then transferred to Jiangxia.

value.zh: 中朝公輔，多非理終，瓘功德不殊，亦無緣獨受偏賞，宜復本封，以正國章。」
value.en: Many grandees and assistants of the central court did not meet a natural end; Guan's merit and virtue were not exceptional, and there is no reason he alone should keep a partial reward—his original enfeoffment should be restored to set the state's regulations right."
value.literal: Many grandees and assistants of the central court did not die natural deaths; Guan's merit and virtue were not exceptional, and there is no reason he alone should receive a partial reward—his original enfeoffment should be restored to rectify the state's regulations."

value.zh: 詔付門下。
value.en: An edict referred the memorial to the Gate Department.
value.literal: An edict referred it to the Gate Department.

value.zh: 前散騎常侍江夏公衛璵上表自陳曰：「臣乃祖故太保瓘，於魏咸熙之中，太祖文皇帝為元輔之日，封蕭陽侯；
value.en: The former supernumerary palace attendant, Duke of Jiangxia Wei Yu, submitted a memorial in his own name, saying, "My founding ancestor, the late Grand Guardian Guan, in the middle of the Wei period of Xianxi, when the founding Emperor Wen was chief minister, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaoyang;
value.literal: The former Supernumerary Palace Attendant, Duke of Jiangxia Wei Yun, submitted a memorial in his own person, saying: "Your servant's founding ancestor, the late Grand Guardian Guan, in the middle of the Wei period of Xianxi, when the founding Emperor Wen was chief minister, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaoyang;

value.zh: 大晉受禪，進爵為公。
value.en: After the Great Jin received the abdication, his rank was advanced to duke.
value.literal: when the Great Jin received the abdication, his rank was advanced to duke.

value.zh: 歷位太保，揔錄朝政。
value.en: He successively held the post of grand guardian and oversaw the recording of court affairs.
value.literal: He successively held the post of Grand Guardian and oversaw recording of court affairs.

value.zh: 於時賈庶人及諸王用事，忌瓘忠節，故楚王瑋矯詔致禍。
value.en: At that time the commoner Jia and the various princes held power; jealous of Guan's loyal integrity, Prince Wei of Chu forged an edict and brought disaster upon him.
value.literal: At that time the commoner Jia and the various princes held power; jealous of Guan's loyal integrity, Prince Yun of Chu therefore forged an edict and brought disaster upon him.

value.zh: 前朝以瓘秉心忠正，加以伐蜀之勳，故追封蘭陵郡公。
value.en: The former court, seeing that Guan held his heart loyal and upright and added the merit of conquering Shu, therefore posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Lanling Commandery.
value.literal: The former court, because Guan held his heart loyal and upright and added the merit of conquering Shu, therefore posthumously enfeoffed him as Duke of Lanling Commandery.

value.zh: 永嘉之中，東海王越食蘭陵，換封江夏，戶邑如舊。
value.en: In the middle of the Yongjia period, Prince Yue of Donghai took Lanling as his sustenance and exchanged the enfeoffment for Jiangxia, with households and fief left unchanged.
value.literal: In the middle of the Yongjia period, Prince Yue of Donghai consumed Lanling and exchanged the enfeoffment for Jiangxia, with households and fief unchanged.

value.zh: 臣高祖散騎侍郎璪，囗之嫡孫，纂承封爵。
value.en: My founding ancestor, Supernumerary Palace Attendant Sao, was the legitimate grandson of [text damaged] and inherited the enfeoffment.
value.literal: Your servant's founding ancestor the Supernumerary Palace Attendant Sao was Guan's legitimate grandson and inherited the enfeoffment.

value.zh: 中宗元皇帝以曾祖故右衛將軍崇承襲，逮于臣身。
value.en: The Central Ancestor, Emperor Yuan, because of my great-grandfather the late Right Colonel of the Guard Chong, continued the succession down to my own person.
value.literal: The Central Ancestor, Emperor Yuan, because of his founding ancestor the Right Colonel of the Guard Chong, continued the succession down to your servant's person.

value.zh: 伏聞祠部郎荀伯子表，欲貶降復封蕭陽。
value.en: I have heard that gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized, wishing to demote and restore the enfeoffment to Xiaoyang.
value.literal: I have heard that Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized, wishing to demote and restore the enfeoffment to Xiaoyang.

value.zh: 夫趙氏之忠，寵延累葉，漢祖開封，誓以山河。
value.en: Zhao's loyalty won favor through successive generations; when the Han founder opened enfeoffments, he bound them with oaths of mountains and rivers.
value.literal: The loyalty of the Zhao clan extended favor through successive generations; when the Han founder opened enfeoffments, he swore them with mountains and rivers.

value.zh: 伏願陛下錄既往之勳，垂罔極之施，乞出臣表，付外參詳。」
value.en: I humbly beg Your Majesty to record past merit and extend boundless favor, and to take my memorial out and refer it outside for joint deliberation."
value.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to record past merit and extend immeasurable favor; I beg that my memorial be taken out and referred outside for joint deliberation."

value.zh: 潁川陳茂先亦上表曰：「祠部郎荀伯子表臣七世祖太尉准禍加淮南，不應濫賞。
value.en: Chen Maoxian of Yingchuan also submitted a memorial, saying, "Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized that my seventh-generation ancestor the Grand Marshal Huai suffered disaster in Huainan and should not have received a reckless reward.
value.literal: Chen Maoxian of Yingchuan also submitted a memorial, saying: "Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites Bozi memorialized that your servant's seventh-generation ancestor the Grand Marshal Huai suffered disaster in Huainan and should not have received a reckless reward.

value.zh: 尋先臣以剪除賈謐，封海陵公，事在淮南遇禍之前。
value.en: I find that my founding ancestor, for cutting down Jia Mi, was enfeoffed as Duke of Hailing—this occurred before Huainan met with disaster.
value.literal: I examine that my founding ancestor, for cutting down Jia Mi, was enfeoffed as Duke of Hailing—this occurred before Huainan met with disaster.

value.zh: 後廣陵雖在擾攘之際，臣祖乃始蒙殊遇，歷位元、凱。
value.en: Later, though Guangling was in a time of turmoil, my grandfather only then received special favor and successively held posts among the foremost.
value.literal: Later, though Guangling was in a time of turmoil, your servant's grandfather only then received special favor and successively held posts among the foremost.

value.zh: 後被遠外，乃作平州，而猶不至除國。
value.en: Afterward he was sent far abroad and made governor of Ping Province, yet the state was still not abolished.
value.literal: Afterward he was sent far abroad and became governor of Ping Province, yet the state was still not abolished.

value.zh: 良以先勳深重，百世不泯故也。
value.en: This was truly because the founding merit was weighty and could not be extinguished for a hundred generations.
value.literal: Truly because the founding merit was weighty and could not be extinguished for a hundred generations.

value.zh: 聖明御世，英輔係興，曾無疑議，以為濫賞。
value.en: Under sage clarity governing the age, worthy assistants arose in succession, and never was there doubt that the grant had been reckless.
value.literal: Under sage clarity governing the age, worthy assistants arose in succession; never was there doubt that it was a reckless reward.

value.zh: 臣以微弱，未齒人倫，加始勉視息，封爵兼嗣。
value.en: I, being slight and weak, have not yet taken my place among men; moreover I have only just barely drawn breath and inherited the enfeoffment by succession.
value.literal: Your servant, being slight and weak, has not yet taken his place among men; moreover he has only just barely drawn breath and inherited the enfeoffment by succession.

value.zh: 伏願陛下遠錄舊勳，特垂矜察。」
value.en: I humbly beg Your Majesty to look back upon the old merit from afar and especially bestow compassionate scrutiny."
value.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to record the old merit from afar and especially bestow compassionate scrutiny.

value.zh: 詔皆付門下，並不施行。
value.en: Edicts referred all memorials to the Gate Department, and none was implemented.
value.literal: Edicts referred all to the Gate Department, and none was implemented.

value.zh: 昔黃帝有子二十五人，或內列諸華，或外分荒服，昌意少子，受封北土，國有大鮮卑山，因以為號。
value.en: Long ago the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons: some served within the Chinese heartland, others were sent to govern the outer marches. Changyi, his youngest, was enfeoffed in the north, where the great Xianbei Mountain stood—and from that mountain the people took their name.
value.literal: In olden times the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons; some were enrolled within the Chinese domains, some were apportioned to distant borderlands. Changyi was his youngest son; he received a fief in the northern lands. The state had the great Xianbei Mountain, and from it took its name.

value.zh: 其後，世為君長，統幽都之北，廣漠之野，畜牧遷徙，射獵為業，淳樸為俗，簡易為化，不為文字，刻木紀契而已，世事遠近，人相傳授，如史官之紀錄焉。
value.en: Afterward they ruled generation upon generation north of Youdu, across the wide steppe. They lived by herding, moving with the seasons, and by the hunt; their ways were plain, their customs unadorned. They had no script—only notches cut in wood to seal bargains. What happened near and far was handed down mouth to mouth, much as if scribes had kept annals.
value.literal: Thereafter generation after generation they were chieftains, ruling north of Youdu in the vast deserts. Pastoral migration and hunting were their livelihood; simplicity their custom, plainness their transformation. They did not use writing, but only carved wood to record agreements. Affairs near and far were passed from person to person, like the records of historians.

value.zh: 黃帝以土德王，北俗謂土為托，謂后為跋，故以為氏。
value.en: The Yellow Emperor reigned under the virtue of Earth; northerners called earth tuo and called a queen ba—so the clan took the name Tuoba.
value.literal: The Yellow Emperor ruled by the virtue of Earth; in northern custom earth was called tuo and a queen was called ba, hence they took it as their clan name.

value.zh: 其裔始均，入仕堯世，逐女魃於弱水之北，民賴其勤，帝舜嘉之，命為田祖。
value.en: A descendant, Shijun, served in the reign of Yao, driving the drought demon Nüba beyond the Weak Water. The people owed their relief to his labor; Shun commended him and named him Lord of the Fields.
value.literal: His descendant Shijun entered service in the age of Yao, drove Nüba north of the Weak Water; the people relied on his diligence, Emperor Shun praised him, and appointed him Lord of the Fields.

value.zh: 爰歷三代，以及秦漢，獯鬻、獫狁、山戎、匈奴之屬，累代殘暴，作害中州，而始均之裔，不交南夏，是以載籍無聞焉。
value.en: Through the Three Dynasties and on into Qin and Han, the Xiongnu and their kindred peoples—Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong—ravaged the Central Plains generation after generation. Yet Shijun's line never dealt with the southern realms, and so the written histories say nothing of them.
value.literal: Thus through the Three Dynasties down to Qin and Han, the Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong, Xiongnu and their kind were generation after generation violent, harming the Central States—but the descendants of Shijun did not mingle with Southern Xia, and therefore they go unmentioned in written records.

value.zh: 五十六年，帝復如晉；
value.en: In the fifty-sixth year the prince again went to Jin;
value.literal: In the fifty-sixth year, the emperor again went to Jin;

value.zh: 其年冬，還國。
value.en: and that winter came home to the realm.
value.literal: that winter he returned to the state.

value.zh: 晉遺帝錦、罽、繒、綵、綿、絹、諸物，咸出豐厚，車牛百乘。
value.en: Jin sent him brocade, felt, silk, dyed cloth, cotton, gauze—gifts in lavish profusion, and a hundred ox-carts besides.
value.literal: Jin presented the emperor brocade, felt, silk, colored silks, cotton, gauze—all manner of goods, lavishly generous, a hundred cartloads of cattle and oxen.

value.zh: 行達并州，晉征北將軍衞瓘，以帝為人雄異，恐為後患，乃密啟晉帝，請留不遣。
value.en: At Bingzhou, Jin's northern commander Wei Guan saw in the prince a man of singular power and feared trouble later on. He secretly memorialized the Jin throne to hold him and not let him go.
value.literal: When the journey reached Bingzhou, Jin's General Who Conquers the North Wei Guan, because the emperor was a man of heroic singularity, feared he would be a later trouble—thereupon secretly memorialized the Jin emperor requesting to detain him and not send him on.

value.zh: 晉帝難於失信，不許。
value.en: The Jin emperor would not break his word and refused.
value.literal: The Jin emperor found it hard to break faith and did not consent.

value.zh: 瓘復請以金錦賂國之大人，令致間隙，使相危害。
value.en: Wei Guan asked again to buy off the realm's chiefs with gold and brocade, sowing discord so they would turn on one another.
value.literal: Wei Guan again requested to use gold and brocade to bribe the state's great chiefs, causing them to sow discord so that they would harm one another.

value.zh: 晉帝從之，遂留帝。
value.en: The Jin emperor agreed, and so the prince was kept.
value.literal: The Jin emperor assented and thus detained the emperor.

value.zh: 於是國之執事及外部大人，皆受瓘貨。
value.en: Then the court officers and the outer chiefs all took Wei Guan's gifts.
value.literal: Thereupon the state's executives and the outer great chiefs all received Wei Guan's bribes.

value.zh: 五十八年，方遣帝。
value.en: In the fifty-eighth year they at last let the prince go.
value.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, they finally sent the emperor off.

value.zh: 始祖聞帝歸，大悅，使諸部大人詣陰館迎之。
value.en: When the Founding Ancestor learned the prince was coming home he rejoiced and sent chiefs of every tribe to Yin Lodge to welcome him.
value.literal: When the Founding Ancestor heard the emperor was returning he was greatly pleased and sent great chiefs of various tribes to Yin Lodge to welcome him.

value.zh: 酒酣，帝仰視飛鳥，謂諸大人曰：「我為汝曹取之。」
value.en: As the wine deepened, the prince looked up at birds on the wing and told the chiefs: "I will fetch those down for you."
value.literal: When the wine had gone deep, the emperor looked up at birds in flight and said to the great chiefs: "I will take them for you all."

value.zh: 援彈飛丸，應弦而落。
value.en: He took up a pellet bow and shot; at the snap of the string the birds dropped.
value.literal: He took up his pellet-bow and flying pellets; at the twang of the string they fell.

value.zh: 時國俗無彈，眾咸大驚，乃相謂曰：「太子風彩被服，同於南夏，兼奇術絕世，若繼國統，變易舊俗，吾等必不得志，不若在國諸子，習本淳樸。」
value.en: The realm had never known the pellet bow; all were astonished and whispered: "The crown prince dresses and carries himself like the southern Chinese, and his uncanny skill has no match. If he inherits the throne and changes our ways, we shall lose our standing. Better a son raised here, steeped in our old simplicity."
value.literal: At that time the state custom had no pellet-bows; the multitude was greatly startled and said among themselves: "The crown prince's manner and dress are like those of Southern Xia, and his strange arts surpass the world—if he inherits the state succession and alters the old customs, we shall certainly not get our way; better the sons within the state, who are versed in our native simplicity."

value.zh: 咸以為然。
value.en: They were agreed.
value.literal: All thought this right.

value.zh: 且離間素行，乃謀危害，並先馳還。
value.en: The seeds of division Wei Guan had planted were already ripe; they plotted against the prince and raced home ahead of him.
value.literal: Moreover the discord sown for many years—thereupon they plotted harm, and all galloped ahead to return first.

value.zh: 始祖問曰：「我子既歷他國，進德何如？」
value.en: The Founding Ancestor asked: "My son has lived in a foreign land—how has his character grown?"
value.literal: The Founding Ancestor asked: "My son, having passed through another state—how has his virtue advanced?"

value.zh: 皆對曰：「太子才藝非常，引空弓而落飛鳥，是似得晉人異法怪術，亂國害民之兆，惟願察之。」
value.en: They answered: "The crown prince's gifts are beyond the common run. He drew an empty bow and felled a bird in flight—as if he had learned Jin sorcery. It is an omen of chaos and harm to the people. We beg Your Majesty to look into this."
value.literal: All replied: "The crown prince's talent is extraordinary; drawing an empty bow he brought down a flying bird—that is as if he had obtained Jin men's strange methods and occult arts, a portent of disordering the state and harming the people. We wish Your Majesty would examine this."

value.zh: 自帝在晉之後，諸子愛寵日進，始祖年踰期頤，頗有所惑，聞諸大人之語，意乃有疑。
value.en: Since the prince had gone to Jin, the other sons had won favor day by day. The Founding Ancestor was past a hundred and his mind was clouded; hearing the chiefs, he began to doubt.
value.literal: From the time the prince had been in Jin, the love and favor toward the other sons daily grew; the Founding Ancestor, more than a hundred years old, was somewhat confused; hearing the great chiefs' words, his mind came to harbor doubt.

value.zh: 因曰：「不可容者，便當除之。」
value.en: He said: "If he cannot be borne, then do away with him."
value.literal: He said: "Whoever cannot be tolerated—just remove him."

value.zh: 於是諸大人乃馳詣塞南，矯害帝。
value.en: The chiefs galloped south of the frontier passes and, by forged order, killed the prince.
value.literal: Thereupon the great chiefs galloped to the south of the passes and, by forged command, killed the emperor.

value.zh: 既而，始祖甚悔之。
value.en: Soon after, the Founding Ancestor was filled with remorse.
value.literal: Before long the Founding Ancestor deeply regretted it.

value.zh: 帝身長八尺，英姿瓌偉，在晉之日，朝士英俊多與親善，雅為人物歸仰。
value.en: The prince stood eight feet tall, splendid in bearing. In Jin many of the court's finest men befriended him; men of the age looked up to him.
value.literal: The emperor stood eight feet in height, heroic and magnificent in bearing; during his days in Jin many of the court's gifted men were fond of him—he was esteemed among men of the age.

value.zh: 後乃追諡焉。
value.en: Later he was given a posthumous title.
value.literal: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed with a title.

value.zh: 其年，始祖不豫。
value.en: That year, the Founding Ancestor fell ill.
value.literal: That year, the Founding Ancestor was unwell.

value.zh: 烏丸王庫賢，親近任勢，先受衞瓘之貨，故欲沮動諸部，因在庭中礪鉞斧，諸大人問欲何為，答曰：「上恨汝曹讒殺太子，今欲盡收諸大人長子殺之。」
value.en: Kuxian, King of the Wuwan, was close to the ruler and used his influence. Having already accepted Wei Guan's bribes, he wanted to alarm the tribes, so he sharpened an axe in the courtyard. When the chiefs asked what he was doing, he said, "The sovereign hates you for slandering and killing the crown prince. Now he intends to seize every chief's eldest son and kill them."
value.literal: Kuxian, King of the Wuwan, was intimate with him and relied on his influence. He had earlier accepted Wei Guan's bribes, and so wished to unsettle the tribes. He therefore sharpened an axe in the courtyard. When the chiefs asked what he intended to do, he replied: "The sovereign resents you all for slandering and killing the crown prince; now he wishes to seize the eldest sons of all the chiefs and kill them."

value.zh: 大人皆信，各各散走。
value.en: The chiefs all believed him and scattered in flight.
value.literal: The chiefs all believed him and scattered in flight one by one.

value.zh: 始祖尋崩。
value.en: The Founding Ancestor soon died.
value.literal: The Founding Ancestor soon died.

value.zh: 凡饗國五十八年，年一百四歲。
value.en: In all, he reigned fifty-eight years and lived to one hundred and four.
value.literal: In all, he enjoyed the state for fifty-eight years and was one hundred and four years old.

value.zh: 太祖即位，尊為始祖。
value.en: When Taizu ascended the throne, he honored him as the Founding Ancestor.
value.literal: When Taizu ascended the throne, he honored him as the Founding Ancestor.

value.zh: 燕鳳 許謙 張袞 崔玄伯 鄧淵
value.en: Biographies of Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Zhang Gun, Cui Xuanbo, and Deng Yuan
value.literal: Yan Feng; Xu Qian; Zhang Gun; Cui Xuanbo; Deng Yuan

value.zh: 玄伯自非朝廷文誥，四方書檄，初不染翰，故世無遺文。
value.en: Unless for court edicts or letters to the four quarters, Xuanbo never took up the brush — and so no writings of his survive.
value.literal: Unless for court documents of the throne or letters to the four directions, Xuanbo never touched the brush — hence no writings survive in the world.

value.zh: 尤善草隸行押之書，為世摹楷。
value.en: He excelled above all in cursive, clerical, running, and draft script, and the age copied him as its model.
value.literal: He was especially skilled in cursive, clerical, running, and draft script — models for the age.

value.zh: 玄伯祖悅與范陽盧諶，並以博藝著名。
value.en: Xuanbo's grandfather Yue and Fanyang's Lu Chen were both famed for wide learning in the arts.
value.literal: Xuanbo's grandfather Yue and Fanyang Lu Chen were both famed for broad arts.

value.zh: 諶法鍾繇，悅法衞瓘，而俱習索靖之草，皆盡其妙。
value.en: Chen took Zhong You as his model, Yue took Wei Guan, and both studied Su Jing's cursive until each reached its utmost subtlety.
value.literal: Chen learned from Zhong You, Yue from Wei Guan, and both studied Su Jing's cursive — each attaining the utmost subtlety.

value.zh: 諶傳子偃，偃傳子邈；
value.en: Chen passed the art to his son Yan, Yan to his son Miao;
value.literal: Chen passed it to his son Yan, Yan to his son Miao;

value.zh: 悅傳子潛，潛傳玄伯。
value.en: Yue passed it to his son Qian, Qian to Xuanbo — so the record runs.
value.literal: Yue passed it to his son Qian, Qian to Xuanbo.

value.zh: 世不替業。
value.en: The craft never failed from father to son.
value.literal: The craft was never broken through the generations.

value.zh: 故魏初重崔盧之書。
value.en: Hence in early Wei the scripts of the Cui and Lu houses were held in highest esteem.
value.literal: Hence in early Wei the scripts of the Cui and Lu houses were prized.

value.zh: 又玄伯之行押，特盡精巧，而不見遺迹。
value.en: Xuanbo's running-draft hand too was wrought to rare refinement, yet no trace of it remains.
value.literal: Xuanbo's running-draft script too was especially refined and ingenious, yet no traces survive.

value.zh: 子浩，襲爵，別有傳。
value.en: His son Hao inherited the title and has a separate biography.
value.literal: His son Hao inherited the title; he is treated in a separate biography.
